articles.title: NFL Trade Deadline: Who Were Biggest Winners, Losers? League Execs React To Top Deals
articles.summary: From the Kirk Cousins deal to the biggest winners and losers, NFL execs dish on this year's trade deadline.
articles.body: NFL trade deadline day didn't spark a ton of fireworks, but plenty of fireworks were shot off in the days and weeks leading up to Tuesday. Of the deals that were made on deadline day, though, none were bigger than the Minnesota Vikings' decision to reunite with Kirk Cousins. The Vikings gave up a third-round pick to land Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders as their quarterback struggles were clearly holding them back. Other moves, like the massive trades the Jacksonville Jaguars made on Monday or the deal the Chicago Bears swung two weeks ago, could define this season's homestretch and postseason. And on the flip side, the Indianapolis Colts and Philadelphia Eagles waved the white flag on the season, securing major draft capital. So, what should we make of the biggest trade deadline deals? Who won and lost the trade deadline? We asked those questions to general managers, executives and scouts around the league. Here's what we learned. Kirk Cousins Trade A Win-Win? Eric D. Williams: While giving Minnesota props for securing a quality quarterback at the trade deadline, an NFL contract negotiator also questioned the team’s personnel department in evaluating previous quarterback decisions and their fit in head coach Kevin O’Connell’s system. "It’s crazy how expectations can spiral so quickly," the league source told me. "And I mean this more so in regard to Kyler Murray. Going into the season, the expectation was that Kyler was the high-ceiling QB who could return O’Connell’s offense to prominence. But from a pro scouting standpoint, the Minnesota front office clearly missed. And now they’re without a third-round pick. "Good for them for cutting their losses and acquiring Cousins, but it’s clear that the Murray signing [while not costing them hardly any money] was a swing and a miss." The contract negotiator sees Cousins as a clear upgrade, but questioned whether the 38-year-old can stay healthy enough to help lead the Vikings on a deep postseason run, considering his past injury history. "I’m not going to discredit what Cousins can do for Minnesota," the league source told me. "With how that defense is playing, Cousins’ acquisition could also fall in the ‘shooting our shot’ bucket. "They just need him to be competent in KOC’s offense. They don’t need him to play hero ball. If he can just run the offense, then they’ll have a chance. But yes, health is a concern." Another league source told me Daniel Jones would have been a better fit if available, but overall liked the trade. "I wish they could have picked up Daniel, but I understand their thinking," the league source said. "And if the MNF game had gone well, they would not have done anything." Ralph Vacchiano: For the most part, this is being viewed as a classic win-win trade, to varying degrees. For the Vikings, the win is obvious: They found what might be the perfect starting QB for them, and it "only" cost them a third-round pick. "I mean, they were desperate," one NFL general manager told me. "They were calling everybody. And they had to do it. [Kyler] Murray and [Carson] Wentz had been terrible. They were going to cost them a real chance at a Super Bowl. I would’ve held out for a second, at least, and I think they would’ve had to pay it. They weren’t coming out of this without a quarterback." They also got what another NFL executive told me was the "perfect guy for them" — a former Viking who knows Kevin O’Connell’s offense and No. 1 wide receiver Justin Jefferson and won’t need long to get up to speed. "If you think about it, it’s kind of a miracle," the executive told me. "The right guy at the right price, and he’s available halfway through the season. What are the odds it works out like that?" As for the Raiders, the general manager summed up their win like this: "They got a 3 for a guy they were going to bench soon anyway. Maybe they have to turn to Fernando Mendoza (their rookie No. 1 overall pick) a little earlier than they wanted. But it was coming soon anyway. Their future is the kid, not the old man. And now they got a Day 2 pick to help the rebuild, too." Were The Colts Smart To Keep Jonathan Taylor? Williams: Both league sources I spoke with about Taylor being on the trade market were not surprised the elite running back stayed in Indianapolis. "I don’t know why the Colts would have traded Taylor at all unless they received a crazy offer," an NFL agent told me. "A new GM and coach would want him. He is 27 and under contract for two years. He just did an extension, so trading him borders on asinine. The Colts could get going the rest of the way. The schedule is reasonable to do so." Another league source I talked with believes the Colts are holding Taylor hostage by keeping him on a losing roster that’s tanking the rest of the season. "People lose sight that the players in the locker room are humans," the league source told me. "With everything over the last two weeks pointing to Taylor moving on and him effectively saying his goodbyes after their last game, it was the absolute wrong thing for them to do by not moving him. "I’m hoping he comes up with a mysterious injury that puts him on IR for the rest of the season, and then they move him in the offseason. That would be the right thing to do." Vacchiano: I thought the Colts made the right decision, but I didn’t find many people who agreed with me. Most of my sources saw the decision as a "surprise," and they believed the Colts were going to take the best offer they had, which was believed to be a second-round pick plus a fourth- or fifth-round pick too. "That’s a good deal for a running back," one NFL source told me. "They are in a total rebuild. They sold a bunch of their best players. They have huge questions about their offensive line and quarterback. They’re going to have a new GM soon, and maybe a coach. And they’re holding on to a 27-year-old running back as the centerpiece of their rebuilding? Who does that?" "Taylor is a great player if he’s on a good team," an AFC scout told me. "The Colts won’t be good again for a while, which makes him dead weight. They should’ve taken the 2-plus, fixed their line, and just replaced him with someone younger." "I was shocked," the general manager told me. "Really thought he was gone. I love [Taylor], but I don’t know what they’re thinking. And I wouldn’t be shocked if the new GM tries to trade him in the offseason before free agency starts." Bears, Eagles Among Biggest Winners Williams: The Chicago Bears and Jacksonville Jaguars are the biggest winners from the moves they made at this year’s trade deadline, according to league sources I spoke with. "I think Chicago and Jacksonville benefited the most," a league source told me. "They are clearly shooting their shot for a Super Bowl appearance this year." The Bears, of course, supercharged their defense with the addition of Defensive Player of the Year candidate Jeffery Simmons. Meanwhile, the Jaguars also addressed their deficiencies on defense by adding safety Jesse Bates, along with defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. Chicago and Jacksonville have two of the best offenses in the league, led by Caleb Williams and Trevor Lawrence, respectively. We’ll see if the defensive upgrades push them over the edge to becoming legitimate Super Bowl contenders at the end of the year. One national scout said the Jaguars could be the biggest winners or biggest losers with their "F’ them picks" approach to trading premium picks for premium players, like the Los Angeles Rams. And that makes sense, with general manager James Gladstone and head coach Liam Coen both having spent time in Los Angeles. "The Jaguars might be the biggest winner and loser," the scout told me. "They went all in and if they win it all, then it’s a win. Or they could lose! But I like the aggressive approach because I think the race is wide open." Vacchiano: Three teams kept coming up in my discussions with league sources: The Vikings, Jaguars and the Eagles, though a few did praise the Colts and Bears, too. The Vikings praise was all about the Kirk Cousins deal. "Finding a QB who can be the difference between making the Super Bowl or not is a huge win no matter how you look at it," one NFL executive told me. "And at that price? Wow. I guarantee they would’ve given up more." The Jaguars earned praise for "going for it all," in the words of one GM. "I don’t love all their deals or what they paid," he told me, "but good for them not sitting still. There’s a reason they say ‘Fortune favors the bold’. And they were bold." The Jaguars were already loaded on offense, but added Bates, Davis and Godchaux at the deadline. "They were already a good defense," an AFC scout told me. "They made it stronger." The only question was about the price they paid for Davis, which included sending a first-round pick to the Eagles. Two sources told me that was "Way too steep." And that’s a big reason why Eagles general manager Howie Roseman was one of the winners. They had already dealt center Cam Jurgens to Baltimore for a second-round pick, and for Davis they got a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick, giving them 10 picks in the first two rounds over the next three drafts. "I’m a little surprised they didn’t do more," one general manager told me. "But they did great. They always do." The Bears, meanwhile, earned praise for acquiring Jeffrey Simmons, whom one scout told me was "the only true difference-making defensive player available." The price was high — two first-round picks. "But again," the general manager told me, "Good teams go for it. They don’t sit still." As for the Colts, despite all the questions about not trading Taylor, they did ship off guard Quenton Nelson, defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and wide receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, trading four players on expiring contracts for a third, two fourths, two fifths and a sixth. "Those may not seem like huge deals," one league executive told me. "But they add up. Better than letting them walk away for nothing." Chargers, Bengals Among Biggest Losers Williams: League sources pointed to the Indianapolis Colts as the clear losers here, giving up Quenton Nelson, Josh Downs, DeForest Buckner and Keenan Allen in a fire sale before the trade deadline. The Colts had moved on from general manager Chris Ballard, so interim general manager Ed Dodds orchestrated the moves, with the blessing of owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon. We’ll see if head coach Shane Steichen remains around at season’s end to clean up the mess. One source told me the Colts should have emptied the tank and moved on from running back Jonathan Taylor. "Indianapolis is the biggest loser by not moving Taylor and taking the reported second and fifth offered for him," the league source told me. Vacchiano: No team has taken more of a deserved beating from NFL sources around the trade deadline than the Los Angeles Chargers, who had even let teams know they were standing pat despite being 0-8 and generally a mess. They did make one deal — sending linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Broncos for a fourth- and fifth-round pick. But that was it. And then, late Wednesday night, that trade fell apart anyway. "Don’t get me started," an NFL executive told me. "Complete malpractice. They weren’t even willing to listen." "Dumbest thing I’ve seen in years," another executive told me. "I don’t know what they’re thinking. They like their players? Great. They’re doing a bang-up job for them." They almost certainly could have gotten something for players like edge rusher Khalil Mack, wide receiver Quentin Johnston and cornerback Donte Jackson, and maybe more. "But they’re sleeping," one of the NFL executives told me. "I really think nobody is home." Another loser: The Washington Commanders. But it wasn’t their fault. They had a lot of interest in defensive tackle Daron Payne, according to sources, including from the New York Giants. But Payne got hurt, ending that. "I wonder if they would’ve dealt WR Terry McLaurin before he got hurt, too," the source said. "A lot of people were looking for receivers." One other loser: The Cincinnati Bengals, "mostly for incompetence," the general manager told me. They had a deal in place with Philadelphia for depth edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie. Then a reporter on social media revealed the move would’ve meant they’d also lose a compensatory third-round pick in the next draft, and the Bengals quickly backed out of the deal. "Embarrassing," the GM told me. "How did they not know that? There are people in every organization whose job, literally, is to figure that stuff out." "I guess it’s good they found out before they lost the comp pick," an NFL executive told me. "But that’s a terrible look." It also didn’t help the Bengals’ cause that the Ebiketie deal was the only one they were apparently considering, despite a struggling defense that is holding them back. "Nobody ever accused the Bengals of being smart," one source told me.

articles.title: Eagles Predicted to Replace Jalen Hurts With Dynamic Quarterback
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles have a major question looming over the head of the franchise. Jalen Hurts has a very uncertain future ahead of him following his seri...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles have a major question looming over the head of the franchise. Jalen Hurts has a very uncertain future ahead of him following his serious blood clot issues this season.

Hurts saw his 2026 season come to an abrupt end due to multiple blood clots. That has led to some speculation that the health issue could end his career.

Whether or not that will be the case remains to be seen. However, the speculation has caused analysts to look at potential replacement options. If the Eagles need to replace Hurts this coming offseason, there are quite a few routes they could explore.

One of those routes will be the 2027 NFL Draft. Philadelphia will have two first-round picks, its own and the Jacksonville Jaguars' first-round selection. That should give the Eagles plenty of ammunition to bring in a new signal caller if they choose to do so.

A new suggestion has been made that would see Philadelphia bring in a long-term replacement for Hurts in the form of a dual-threat quarterback.

Philadelphia Eagles Predicted to Add Dynamic QB as Potential Jalen Hurts Successor

Bleacher Report's Brent Sobleski released a new mock draft on November 11. In that mock draft, he had the Eagles taking LSU offensive tackle Jordan Seaton with the No. 5 overall pick.

With the Jaguars' first-round pick, he has Philadelphia bringing in South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers.

"Once upon a time, Philadelphia Eagles general manager Howie Roseman drafted Jalen Hurts despite Carson Wentz already being on the team's roster and signed to a long-term contract. Less than a year later, Wentz was gone and Hurts became the team's starting quarterback," Sobleski wrote .

"With the uncertainty surrounding Hurts' health and his inconsistent play over the last two seasons, Roseman should strongly consider a similar approach, particularly with an extra first-round pick now in the team's back pocket."

Sellers has played well this season for the Gamecocks. He has completed 62.8 percent of his pass attempts for 2,100 yards, 17 touchdowns, and seven interceptions. On the ground, he has racked up 637 yards and seven more touchdowns.

Hurts is known for his dual-threat ability. Bringing in a quarterback like Sellers would allow the Eagles to continue the same offensive system they have already had in place.

Whether or not Hurts will be back next season remains an unknown. But, if Philadelphia chooses to target a quarterback in the NFL Draft, Sellers could make a lot of sense as a potential fit due to his skill-set and play style.

articles.title: Bruce Arians says Andrew Luck had a rare skill that even Peyton Manning and Tom Brady lacked
articles.summary: Andrew Luck's photographic memory stunned Bruce Arians during his 2012 rookie season, setting the Colts QB apart from Peyton Manning's approach.
articles.body: Andrew Luck’s NFL career was shorter than those of some of his contemporaries. However, the former Colts signal caller left an impression, and according to Bruce Arians, Luck had a certain skillset that some of the best quarterbacks of all time did not even have. And, no, it's not looking like a Civil War general... but he can do that too. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The coaching great did an interview with NFL insider Jordan Schultz, and he talked about coaching Luck during the 2012 season. Arians served as the Indianapolis Colts' offensive coordinator and then interim head coach, stepping in for Chuck Pagano, who stepped away from the team to undergo treatment for leukemia. That season was Luck's rookie year, and Arians quickly realized something about his new QB out of Stanford. "Andrew was like, 'I got it; let's roll,'" Arians recalled. "Andrew Luck had a photographic memory because he didn't take any notes. Peyton (Manning) had notebooks. Tom had a notebook on top of a notebook on top of a notebook." Arians said that he asked Luck why he wasn't taking any notes, with Luck claiming that he didn't need to. "He would literally spit it back verbatim," he said. 'GLAD TO SEE IT': SUPER BOWL CHAMPION BRUCE ARIANS RIPS OUT-OF-CONTROL NFL REFS AFTER TWO SUSPENSIONS Arians also recalled that during that season, when the Colts became known for late, dramatic wins, Luck was ready to spring into action in situations the team had practiced. Even before being called upon. "Lo and behold, that exact scenario happened in our game that Sunday," Arians said. "And Andrew's not even waiting for me; he's already on the field." Arians said that Luck and that Kodak-like brain of his wound up executing to perfection and allowed the Colts to win with a late field goal. Luck has since become the general manager of the Stanford Cardinals football program, while Arians went on to coach the Arizona Cardinals and Tampa Bay Buccaneers, winning a Super Bowl with the latter. In the same interview, Arians expressed his interest in returning to the NFL sidelines after dealing with some health issues. articles.title: "Have the audacity": Taylor Frankie Paul hints at joining Sam Hartman's Bachelor season after her own Bachelorette journey was scrapped
articles.summary: Taylor Frankie Paul appeared ready to give Bachelor Nation another chance after her own season of The Bachelorette was cancelled before its scheduled
articles.body: Taylor Frankie Paul appeared ready to give Bachelor Nation another chance after her own season of The Bachelorette was cancelled before its scheduled premiere. The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star recently caught the attention of fans after expressing interest in new Bachelor lead Sam Hartman. Her playful social media activity suggested that she had not ruled out finding love on television again, even after her previous reality dating opportunity ended amid controversy.Taylor Frankie Paul shows interest in Sam Hartman's Bachelor seasonPaul made her interest clear after ABC announced that Washington Commanders quarterback Sam Hartman would lead the 30th season of The Bachelor. She shared an Instagram Reel featuring Ron Swanson, played by Nick Offerman in Parks and Recreation, submitting a fictional application for the dating show.When the application asked what would make her stand out among the other contestants, Paul offered a cheeky response."Ahhh, I was the first bachelorette in history to be on hold."The joke referred to her own season, which never reached viewers after ABC pulled it from its schedule. She captioned the video, "I chose to have the audacity🌹."Paul also joined the conversation under social media announcements about Hartman's casting. She commented, "Dang sign me up 😍" on Bachelor Nation's post. On another fan account's announcement, she wrote, "well he's cute," making her interest difficult to miss.Her comments came after she had stepped away from The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives in September, adding another change to her reality television career.Sam Hartman admitted he was nervous about becoming The BachelorHartman also faced a major adjustment as he prepared to exchange his football career for a television dating experience. During his November 13 appearance on Good Morning America, the quarterback admitted that meeting 30 women at once would not come naturally to him."I'm excited but also very nervous," Hartman said, adding, "I have a tough time holding conversation with one girl. Thirty is going to be pretty tough."He also revealed that he initially resisted the opportunity."Honestly, at first, I was like, ‘No way,’" he explained.A conversation with host Jesse Palmer, a former Bachelor and NFL player, helped change his mind. Hartman said Palmer offered insight into what the experience involved and what he could expect.The timing also placed Hartman in an unusual position. He became the franchise's first lead after Paul's cancelled season, which had been scheduled to premiere in March 2026 following the resurfacing of footage from a 2023 domestic violence incident.Season 30 of The Bachelor was scheduled to premiere on March 21, 2027, at 8 p.m. ET/PT on ABC, with episodes available on Hulu the following day.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jalen Hurts' Blood Clots Investigation Outlined By NFL in New Letter to US Senator
articles.summary: The NFL sent more details regarding the upcoming joint review of Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts' blood clots as well as its protocols for tracking blood clots in response to an inquiry from U.S. Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester, per ESPN's Tim McManus.
articles.body:
The NFL sent more details regarding the upcoming joint review of Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts' blood clots as well as its protocols for tracking blood clots in response to an inquiry from U.S. Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester, per ESPN's Tim McManus .

"As outlined by the league and NFLPA's Collective Bargaining Agreement, mutually agreed-upon independent medical experts will review the matter and share their conclusions and recommendations with both parties," NFL executive vice president of communications, public affairs and health policy Jeff Miller said in a statement released Friday, via McManus.

"The League and Players Association also have several medical committees that review and monitor player injury data closely," he added. "For at least the past decade, the NFL has tracked clotting disorders among players every season through a subcommittee of its General Medical Committee, and this information is shared with the NFLPA. Following the ongoing joint review, the League and NFLPA will consider appropriate next steps, including whether this case points to a need for additional league-wide guidance."

Hurts was previously ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 NFL season after he was diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli.

According to Jonathan Jones of The Athletic, Philadelphia's medical staff discovered a superficial blood clot in Hurts' calf after flying to London for a Week 5 matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Hurts ended up playing against Jacksonville before it was announced that he would be sidelined for the remainder of the year.

The NFL Players Association eventually called for a full investigation of the situation on Oct. 20 before the NFL and NFLPA announced that an investigation would be conducted five days later.

McManus noted Friday that the examination of Hurts and the Eagles by independent medical experts has yet to begin, although the joint review appears to be on the horizon.

articles.title: “I learned to be who I wanted to be”: How Donna Kelce's Ohio University years changed her life before Jason and Travis Kelce became the popular NFL stars
articles.summary: Long before Jason and Travis Kelce became NFL stars, their mother, Donna Kelce, was a young woman trying to find her own identity.
articles.body: Long before Jason and Travis Kelce became NFL stars, their mother, Donna Kelce, was a young woman trying to find her own identity. She grew up in a religious family and described her childhood as sheltered. But leaving home for Ohio University gave her a chance to experience a world she had barely known. From meeting people with different backgrounds to discovering her independence, those college years changed how she saw life. Decades later, Donna still looks back on that experience as a turning point.Donna Kelce discovered a whole new world after leaving home for collegeDonna Kelce graduated from Ohio University in 1974 with a degree in radio and television. Her decision to attend the university was partly driven by its campus and its distance from home. She wanted to experience college life without having family members constantly dropping by or making frequent trips home.She later explained that she chose radio and television because it sounded fun. She also enjoyed writing and English, which made the subject a natural choice for her.But college gave her much more than a degree. The Civil Rights Movement and the Vietnam War were shaping conversations across the country during those years. Donna encountered different cultures, music and ideas that challenged the sheltered environment she had known growing up.In an interview with Ohio University News, published on December 18, 2023, she spoke about how much the experience changed her outlook.“I was so sheltered as a child,” Donna said. “Ohio University opened my eyes to everything. I didn’t know anything. I came from a very religious family and was very sheltered. A whole new world opened up to me.”She also used her time at college to discover the kind of person she wanted to become. Donna played intramural basketball and learned to form her own opinions rather than simply follow expectations.“I learned not to just be a cookie cutter individual. I learned to be who I wanted to be,” she said.Her experience was especially significant at a time when women often faced limited expectations about their future. Donna recalled that women were generally encouraged to attend college and marry a man who would graduate. However, her time at Ohio University helped her look beyond those expectations.How Donna Kelce carried her college lessons into her career and motherhoodDonna Kelce did not pursue broadcasting after graduating. Instead, she entered the banking industry and built a career that eventually included vice president and senior vice president positions at banking organisations in Northeast Ohio. She also earned an MBA from Baldwin Wallace University.Despite moving away from the field she studied, Donna never considered her communication degree useless. The skills she developed at Ohio University helped her make presentations, speak in front of people and build professional relationships.During the same interview, she explained why communication played such an important role in her career.“I needed to meet people and be able to connect and relate to individuals,” she said.She also shared a piece of advice that reflected her years of professional experience: “You need to be able to listen, learn, step back and keep your mouth shut.”Those lessons also influenced her approach to parenting. Donna and her former husband, Ed Kelce, encouraged their sons to express their feelings openly. She believes Jason and Travis learned from watching their parents communicate with each other.“They are two extremely articulate men who are very good at expressing their emotions and feelings,” Donna said.Fans can see that side of the brothers on their New Heights podcast. Jason and Travis regularly discuss football, family and personal experiences, often sharing stories that go beyond their careers in the NFL.Donna's college experience happened decades before either son became a professional football player. Yet the independence she discovered at Ohio University and the communication skills she developed stayed with her through banking and motherhood.In Donna’s case, college was not simply about earning a degree. It was the place where she stepped outside the sheltered life she had known and began discovering who she wanted to be.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Cowboys owner Jerry Jones updates timeline for NFL's 18-game schedule, floats preseason reduction
articles.summary: Jerry Jones says the NFL could move to an 18-game schedule as soon as next year, but the NFLPA has vowed to defend player health and safety.
articles.body: The NFL expanded from a 16-game schedule to 17 games in 2021. Since then, speculation has persisted about whether the league will eventually add an 18th regular-season game. Such a change would require negotiations over roster sizes, player salaries, the preseason schedule and the timing of the Super Bowl. The NFL Players Association would also have to approve the plan before it could move forward. But Jerry Jones, one of the NFL’s most high-profile and outspoken owners, offered a timeline Friday for when the league could add another regular-season game. "I don’t think we’re far away from it," Jones told Dallas sports radio station 105.3 FM. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Jones suggested the league could move to an expanded regular season as soon as 2027. "I don’t know what is far away — next month, next year, maybe. Next year, maybe. That has to be negotiated with the players. But it’s in everybody’s best interest." Interest in potentially adding another game to the schedule for each of the NFL’s 32 teams has been fueled by the league’s growing popularity and expanded international schedule. This season features a record nine games played outside the U.S. A 10-game international slate has been approved for 2027. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell has been a vocal supporter of many owners’ push for an 18-game schedule. Jones suggested the preseason could be shortened if the change becomes reality, with teams using the early weeks of the regular season to ramp up. "You’d cut back on the preseason games, you’d have teams more developed in the first few games, the type of thing you were trying to get done in the preseason. It’s in everybody’s interest, and it certainly is in the players’ best interests, in my mind." Jones’ comments suggest an ambitious timeline. The NFL Players Association has expressed mixed feelings about expanding the regular season. In March, NFLPA executive director JC Tretter told The Athletic that the union was determined to "defend our players and their health." ROGER GOODELL DETAILS NFL EXPANSION POSSIBILITIES AND A TIMETABLE FOR A FULL SEASON OF INTERNATIONAL GAMES "There are things that are not good for our players that we need to make sure we’re protecting them from," Tretter said. "And as of right now, those are all subjects of bargaining. The league can’t expand past 10 international games. The league’s at 17 games in the CBA. That is where we’re at, and we’re going to make sure we defend our players and their health and safety because our guys feel they know what this feels like." Tretter, a former offensive lineman, spent eight seasons in the NFL and last played for the Cleveland Browns in 2021. "I understand what it felt like when I played 16 (games) and then moved to 17," Tretter said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I understand the toll that takes on the body … I understand the same thing with international. I played an international game. I understand the timeline and how tough it is to recover, how tough it is to turn around and get on the flight on the way back and then get ready for the next week. That is not easy." articles.title: Malik Nabers Jokes He 'Can't Answer' Jayden Daniels' Phone Call After Giants' Loss vs. Commanders
articles.summary: Malik Nabers joked his former LSU teammate Jayden Daniels is blowing up his phone after the New York Giants' 24-21 Thursday night loss to the Washington Commanders.
articles.body:
Malik Nabers joked his former LSU teammate Jayden Daniels is blowing up his phone after the New York Giants' 24-21 Thursday night loss to the Washington Commanders.

"It's bugging me pretty bad," Nabers said Friday about losing to Daniels and the Commanders (h/t SNY). "And he's bugging me all the time.

"He's probably trying to call me right now, but I can't answer that phone call."

Nabers still has yet to claim an NFL win over Daniels, who improved Thursday night to 4-0-1 in five career matchups against the Giants.

Daniels started out the matchup by throwing his first two interceptions of the season, but rallied down the stretch to put the Commanders ahead with less than a minute left in regulation.

Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy attempted to answer by finding Nabers on a Hail Mary only to instead throw a game-ending interception to Rasul Douglas.

Nabers and Daniels were teammates at LSU from 2022 to 2023. The pair became NFC East rivals after they were each selected in the first round of the 2024 draft.

Thursday night's loss to Daniels' team might particularly sting for Nabers given that it helped keep the Commanders' playoff hopes alive.

The Giants (5-3-1) still lead the division with the Dallas Cowboys (4-5) in second place, but the Commanders (3-5-1) are within two games of the Giants with a head-to-head tiebreaker in hand.

articles.title: Hailee Steinfeld opens up about first holiday season with Josh Allen's baby, teasing plans that make it extra special
articles.summary: Hailee Steinfeld wants her daughter’s first holiday season to feel special.
articles.body: Hailee Steinfeld wants her daughter’s first holiday season to feel special. The actress, who is married to Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen, told Extra this week that the family has plans to make it that way for Harper Haize, born in April. She kept the details to herself. The calendar is crowded, though. Allen is in the middle of the NFL season, and Steinfeld is promoting her new Disney film, “Hexed,” which hits theaters on November 25. Two demanding jobs and a baby under a year old make for a full schedule.Hailee Steinfeld plans an extra special first holiday season for HarperSteinfeld made the comments while promoting “Hexed” with Extra. Asked about the weeks ahead, she got straight to the point.“This is my first holiday with a baby, though, so we’re excited to make the holidays a little extra special this year,” the actress said.She did not list the plans. She did, however, describe the effort behind them. “The prep and the cooking and all that is, you know… fun until it’s not. It’s a lot of work,” she added. Anyone who has hosted a holiday meal knows the feeling.Support is coming from her co-stars, too. Rashida Jones and Jodie Foster are both moms, and Steinfeld said that has helped. “I’m getting a lot of love and support, which is very needed during this time, but it’s the most incredible thing,” she said. “I feel so so very blessed.”The couple married in Santa Barbara in May 2025, and Harper arrived in April.Steinfeld has been open about the early milestones, including her first Mother’s Day, when she shared photos of Harper holding her hand and a table of cards and a cake.Halloween offered a preview. Last month, the couple threw an “Allen’s in Wonderland” party. Steinfeld and Allen came as the King and Queen of Hearts, and Harper dressed as Alice in a blue dress, white tights and black Mary Jane shoes. A large sign read “We’re All Mad Here.”Allen’s season is in full swing, and Steinfeld has a film to sell. Yet both spent time on a themed Halloween party, which suggests the holidays are a priority, not an afterthought.Steinfeld’s Disney film Hexed opens November 25“Hexed” is a supernatural Disney original. Steinfeld voices Billy, the daughter of Alice, who is played by Jones. Billy is trying to find and balance her magical ability. Walton Goggins, Tracey Ullman and Stephen Fry round out the cast. Steinfeld calls it “a story of self-discovery and one of learning your power.”She also sings on the soundtrack, with a cover of The Cars’ 1980s hit “Magic.” Speaking with Jimmy Fallon in October, she said the role was a “dream come true” and that she “jumped at the opportunity.”The film opens about five weeks before the year ends. Allen still has football to play. And Harper, for her part, has no idea any of this is happening.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “The truth didn’t save me..”: Mike Tomlin revisits $100,000 NFL fine after controversial Jacoby Jones incident against Baltimore Ravens in 2013
articles.summary: Mike Tomlin still remembers the night his actions became one of the biggest talking points of a Steelers-Ravens game.
articles.body: Mike Tomlin still remembers the night his actions became one of the biggest talking points of a Steelers-Ravens game. On December 2, 2013, the Pittsburgh Steelers coach found himself at the center of a controversy involving Baltimore returner Jacoby Jones. The NFL later fined Tomlin $100,000, but he has always maintained that he never tried to interfere with Jones’ kickoff return.After years, Tomlin has offered a closer look at what happened that night. Speaking on the Not Just Football podcast, the Steelers coach explained how watching the stadium's jumbotron left him disoriented and why he moved just before Jones reached the sideline.Mike Tomlin explains why he moved into Jacoby Jones’ path during the 2013 Ravens gameThe incident happened in the third quarter after Pittsburgh scored a touchdown against Baltimore. Jacoby Jones caught the ensuing kickoff and began a long return. As he ran down the sideline, he came dangerously close to Tomlin, who stood near the playing area.The return covered 73 yards, but the attention quickly shifted to the Steelers coach. Television replays showed Tomlin smiling on the jumbotron, adding to the suspicion that he might have deliberately stepped into Jones' path to slow him down.Tomlin offered a different explanation on the Not Just Football podcast. He said he had been watching the kickoff through the stadium screen when he suddenly noticed himself appearing on it."The truth didn't save me from a fine," Tomlin said on the podcast. "I got fined a hundred thousand dollars after the ball was kicked."He also explained that the screen gave him a confusing view of the play."Spatially, I get disoriented where I am and I'm watching something that I don't want to happen," Tomlin recalled. He said he immediately moved to his left after spotting himself on the jumbotron because he feared Jones might run straight into him.His explanation also came down to a routine he followed during kickoff returns.Tomlin told the podcast that he regularly spoke to his kickoff team before they took the field. He would then stand near the yard line where the ball was kicked from to check whether his players were onside. Once the kick happened, he usually watched the play on the stadium screen because it offered an aerial view.However, Baltimore's stadium had only one jumbotron at the time. That made it harder for Tomlin to judge his position while following the return.NFL handed Tomlin a $100,000 fine despite his explanation, while Ben Roethlisberger defended himThe NFL did not accept the incident as an innocent mistake. After reviewing the footage and investigating Tomlin's actions, the league fined him $100,000 for standing too close to the field and interfering with the return.The league believed Tomlin had stepped onto the playing field. Officials considered his actions serious enough to warrant an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty.The Steelers also received a warning that the league could take away draft picks in the 2014 NFL Draft. However, Pittsburgh did not lose any selections.Jones also spoke about the incident after the game. The Ravens returner admitted that Tomlin's presence affected his run, although he took responsibility for not finishing the play."It broke my stride a little bit," Jones said after the game. "(But) I still shouldn't have got caught."Tomlin did receive support from his own quarterback. Ben Roethlisberger defended the coach during a 2013 appearance on 93.7 The Fan, saying he did not believe the move was intentional."I don't think it was intentional," Roethlisberger said. He also explained that he understood why Tomlin watched the jumbotron, as it offered a better view of the action.Interestingly, the controversy did not prevent Tomlin from bringing Jones to Pittsburgh later. In November 2015, the Steelers claimed the wide receiver off waivers.The incident remains a memorable moment from Tomlin's coaching career. More than a decade later, his explanation makes clear that he still disputes the idea that he tried to disrupt Jones' return. The $100,000 fine, however, remains part of the story.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake edges Troy in final seconds for epic Class A football title win
articles.summary: Burnt Hills advances to the state tournament.
articles.body:
COLONIE - The waning stages of the fourth quarter Friday night for the Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake football team were looking painfully dire, as the Spartans found themselves down a point against Troy and forced to give the ball back on a punt.

In a span of a few minutes, BH-BL senior standout Login Tomlinson made two of the biggest plays of his career - the first with his hand and the second with his foot - to flip things back in favor of his team in the Section 2 Class A Super Bowl.

First, Tomlinson forced Troy junior quarterback Kyair Carr to fumble the ball away at the Flying Horses' 23-yard line. Then, BH-BL had just 17 seconds left when it had Tomlinson line up for a 32-yard field goal on third down and without a timeout remaining. The senior - following a timeout by Troy - drilled a go-ahead, line-drive boot down the middle in what ended up being a thrilling 23-21 Super Bowl victory over the Flying Horses at Colonie High School.

"I have been dreaming about this since I was a little kid and first starting kicking," said Tomlinson, a four-year varsity player who is headed to Siena University to play lacrosse. "It happened. It came true."

"It was really nerve-racking out there," BH-BL junior quarterback Tristan West said. "I believed in him every moment when he went out there to kick."

The pulse-pounding triumph secured BH-BL (11-0) the program's 11th Class A sectional title in 20 years, and first since 2021. It also marked the first championship guided by fourth-year coach Kevin DeBonis. The loss denied Troy, playing in its second straight Super Bowl, a 10th title since first winning one in 1993.

"This feels amazing. Since we were little kids, this is what we have been working for," West said.

Last year, the Flying Horses lost to Niskayuna. Troy senior fullback/defensive Ben Mergil, who produced two touchdown receptions and recovered a fumble by BH-BL, emerged from an emotional postgame gathering to put the defeat into context.

"It is hard, but, at the end of the day, it is football," Mergil said. "Anybody that has ever played football knows it will teach life lessons. Sometimes, things just don't shake out for you, but you just have to roll with the punches. I want to thank my coaches, my teammates and God for giving me this opportunity to play for such an amazing school and play my heart out."

Both squads left everything they had on the field. There were colossal swings of momentum swapped between the two teams all evening, especially down the stretch.

Troy led 14-0 and went to halftime up 14-6. West connected with Michael Bies for a 21-yard touchdown pass and Owen Huggins scored on a 2-point conversion to provide BH-BL its first lead at 20-14, but Troy senior running back Nymiear Jenkins - lined up in a wildcat formation - found Mergil on a 6-yard touchdown pass with 3:32 left to tie the score. Troy freshman kicker Crosby Murray booted the extra point through the uprights to provide Troy a 21-20 advantage.

"I really thought when we went ahead, our defense would get the stop and we did," Mergil said. "We went out there to run out the clock and things sometimes don't shake out the way you want."

Troy had the chance to run out the clock after stopping BH-BL and forcing a punt with 2:27 left, but Tomlinson helped set up the game-clinching sequence by punching the ball away from Carr on a first-down run down the Troy sideline.

Tomlinson saved his best for last. Originally summoned to the varsity as a freshman to be a kicker and punter, the senior has excelled at linebacker over the last three years. Friday, he reminded everyone how good of a kicker he is with the biggest field goal of his career.

"That is a hell of a play, and a hell of a player," Mergil said.

"This was a true nail-bitter. We knew Troy was going to be tough to beat and real physical," West said. "We knew it was going to be a close game and it feels great to come out with a 'W.'"

124: Rushing yards turned in by Carr on 21 attempts.

3: Turnovers that Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake committed in the first half.

2: Total field goals this season for Tomlinson after Friday's game-winning kick.

Troy: The season came to a painful close for the Flying Horses with an 8-3 overall record.

Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake: The Spartans return to Colonie High School next Friday for a state quarterfinal contest against Section 9 champion Cornwall (8-3), a 27-26 winner over Washingtonville.

articles.title: ‘All They Care About Is Money,’ ‘There Needs To Be 2 Bye Weeks’ — NFL Fans React as Jerry Jones Argues Proposed 18-Game Season Is in ‘Players’ Best Interest’
articles.summary: Jerry Jones is ready for more regular-season football. His claim that players should also want it proved considerably harder to sell.
articles.body:
Jerry Jones is ready for more regular-season football. His claim that players should also want it proved considerably harder to sell.

The Cowboys owner suggested an 18-game schedule could be approaching, while acknowledging that players would have to negotiate the change, a stance that prompted fans to respond with a mix of enthusiasm, demands for additional rest, and skepticism about who would benefit most.

Jerry Jones Makes His Case for an 18-Game Season

Speaking on 105.3 The Fan, Jones was asked whether an expanded regular season remained far away.

"No, I don't think we're far away from it," he told reporters .

Jones floated next year as a possibility, then acknowledged the necessary negotiations with players. He also proposed reducing preseason games and allowing teams to develop during the opening weeks of the regular season.

"It's in everybody's interest, and it certainly is in the players' best interest in my mind, for sure," Jones said.

"Injuries rising, but they keep adding games because all they care about is money," one fan wrote .

"Is it in 'everyone's' best interests?" sports commentator Brandon Perna asked .

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

"Everyone's best interest except the players lmao," Sleeper's NFL account added .

An additional meaningful game would offer another week of football to watch and sell, while players would have another regular-season assignment to prepare for and compete. The toll on the players, though, is quite another matter altogether.

Some Fans Want More Football With Added Protections

There was a little bit of support for the idea, including one fan ready to go well beyond Jones' proposal.

"Love this.. If the WNBA added 6 games and the NFL 2 games.. Why can't the NFL add 1 more? Make it 20 games! We the fans will watch every week!" the fan wrote .

Others approached the question with conditions.

"There need to be two bye weeks for teams, IR spots need to increase, especially designations to return off of them, there should be an additional active roster spot available as well for gamedays," another fan posted .

Another response acknowledged the financial appeal while questioning the physical consequences. "For the longevity and health of players – no. But it is in everyone's best interest as that extra game will literally earn everyone so much money, including the players," one user wrote .

The request for protections reflects issues already raised in the broader discussion. The NFLPA previously pushed back on treating expansion as inevitable , emphasizing that an additional game is a matter for negotiation.

Commissioner Roger Goodell has also identified roster sizes, player safety and a potential second bye as subjects requiring discussion with the union.

That is where Jones' argument faces its real test.

articles.title: Last-minute fantasy football streaming options for NFL Week 10: Quarterback
articles.summary: Finding a dependable quarterback streamer can be the difference between salvaging a difficult fantasy football matchup and watching your week slip away. With...
articles.body:
Finding a dependable quarterback streamer can be the difference between salvaging a difficult fantasy football matchup and watching your week slip away. With injuries, inconsistent performances, and challenging matchups, Week 10 offers several alternatives for managers looking beyond the usual top-tier starters. Drew Lock headlines this group with an appealing matchup against Las Vegas. Geno Smith and Kirk Cousins offer opportunities for significant passing volume. Deshaun Watson is a deeper-league gamble with additional value through his mobility. If you need a last-minute quarterback replacement , these four options deserve consideration before setting your lineup.

Drew Lock enters Week 10 as one of the more appealing quarterback streaming options. The Seahawks quarterback has quietly operated with impressive poise and efficiency, coming off a 17-3 victory over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9. Seattle's offense did not need to do anything spectacular to secure the win. However, Lock's ability to protect the football and keep the unit moving was encouraging.

The matchup against Las Vegas offers considerably more fantasy upside. The Raiders are coming off a difficult defensive performance in which they surrendered 38 points to the San Francisco 49ers. Their secondary has struggled to contain intermediate passing routes and vertical throws. That should create opportunities for Seattle to exploit favorable matchups downfield.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Playing at Allegiant Stadium also means Lock will have an indoor environment without weather concerns. That could help Seattle's passing attack operate smoothly. If the Raiders struggle to generate pressure or contain Seattle's receivers, Lock could deliver multiple touchdown passes. For managers searching for a relatively safe streaming option, Lock is arguably the most attractive choice in this group.

Geno Smith is another quarterback worth considering, particularly for managers who prioritize passing volume. He faces a challenging divisional matchup against the Buffalo Bills at MetLife Stadium. Buffalo has been playing excellent football, making this a difficult assignment on paper. That said, the expected game script could work in Smith's favor.

The Jets are coming off a disappointing road loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Buffalo enters this contest with momentum after defeating Minnesota. If the Bills establish control early, New York could be forced to abandon its running game and rely heavily on Smith's arm to remain competitive.

Smith has completed 67.5% of his passes this season. He has consistently looked toward Garrett Wilson as a primary downfield target. That connection should remain central to the Jets' offensive approach. A pass-heavy game plan could push Smith beyond 35 attempts. That may create opportunities for substantial yardage and even late-game touchdown production. Smith carries some risk against Buffalo's defense. However, the possibility of a high-volume passing afternoon makes him a reasonable option in deeper leagues.

Kirk Cousins offers another intriguing alternative. He travels to Lambeau Field for an NFC North rivalry game against the Green Bay Packers. Minnesota is coming off a frustrating loss to Buffalo. The matchup against Green Bay, though, could create a different offensive environment. The Packers have an explosive offense of their own, potentially forcing the Vikings to keep pace through the air. That kind of game script could provide Cousins with plenty of opportunities to accumulate passing yards and touchdowns.

Cousins has already thrown 20 touchdown passes this season. His connection with Justin Jefferson here should give Minnesota a reliable downfield weapon. Against Green Bay's defense, Cousins should have opportunities to find openings over the middle and attack coverage gaps.

He is not necessarily a high-ceiling option, but his passing volume and established chemistry with Jefferson make him a worthwhile streamer. A 250-yard performance with multiple touchdowns is within reach.

Deshaun Watson is a more speculative option. That said, his dual-threat ability makes him worth monitoring in deeper fantasy football leagues. Watson hosts the Houston Texans in an AFC matchup that could force Cleveland to become more aggressive offensively.

Houston's explosive offense could put pressure on the Browns to keep pace on the scoreboard. That potentially creates additional passing opportunities for Watson. While the Texans' defensive front presents a difficult challenge, their aggressive pass rush could also create opportunities for Watson to escape pressure and make plays outside the pocket.

His mobility is an important part of his fantasy appeal. Watson can contribute rushing yards when passing opportunities become difficult. That gives him a potential floor that some traditional pocket passers in this ranking tier cannot match. His developing connection with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. also offers another avenue for red-zone production. Watson remains a risky play. However, managers desperate for a quarterback with upside may find his combination of mobility and potential passing volume appealing.

Lock is the top streaming target thanks to his favorable matchup against Las Vegas. Cousins offers passing upside. Smith could benefit from volume. Watson is a deeper-league gamble. Choose according to your roster needs and appetite for risk.

articles.title: Raiders’ Future With Maxx Crosby Gets Major Insider Update
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders continued forward with superstar pass rusher Maxx Crosby on the roster through the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Despite more swirling rumor...
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders continued forward with superstar pass rusher Maxx Crosby on the roster through the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Despite more swirling rumors, Crosby remains with the only franchise he has ever played for since being drafted in 2019.

Crosby was traded during the offseason. The Raiders agreed to a trade with the Baltimore Ravens that would have shipped Crosby out of town in exchange for two first-round picks. When all was said and done, the Ravens decided to pull out of the deal.

Following that decision from Baltimore, Crosby returned to Las Vegas. Both sides opted to move forward together.

While Crosby remains with the Raiders, there are many who don't expect his reunion to be long-term. There are still trade rumors surrounding him for a reason. He remains a top potential trade candidate to watch heading into the 2027 NFL offseason.

Keeping all of that in mind, an NFL insider has offered a new update about Crosby's future in Las Vegas.

Maxx Crosby's Future With Raiders Gets Major Insider Update

According to NFL insider Jason La Canfora, one NFL general manager spoke out and said that he doesn't think Crosby will finish out his current contract with the Raiders.

"He was effectively dealt last March," La Canfora wrote . "That was a done deal to Baltimore as far as the Raiders were concerned. They aren't going to get two first-round picks like the Ravens had on the table, but execs think they can get one, plus a day-two pick."

La Canfora continued on, revealing the quote from the general manager.

"And with that defense still in deep disrepair, the Raiders are going to need to load up on potential young blue-chip players on that side of the ball. They are still going to be two offseasons away from competing. 'I don't think he plays out this contract there,' one GM told me of Crosby in Vegas."

So far this season in Las Vegas, Crosby has played in nine games. He has recorded 26 total tackles, four sacks, a forced fumble, a fumble recovery, and a defended pass. Throughout his entire 119-game NFL career, he has totaled 465 tackles, 73.5 sacks, 12 forced fumbles, four fumble recoveries, an interception, and 30 defended passes.

It will be interesting to see what the future has in store for Crosby and the Raiders. For now, there are many who still think a trade is on the horizon.

articles.title: Deion Sanders, Colorado upset Houston: 'Like we just won the Super Bowl'
articles.summary: Colorado coach Deion Sanders pulled off an upset win at home against Houston Friday night. Does it change the narrative about his job security?
articles.body:
The coaching career of Deion Sanders still has a pulse.

After what happened at Colorado on Friday night Nov. 13, its heart even beats with enough rhythm to potentially reverse the narrative about him with two more games left in the regular season.

Sanders' Colorado football team beat No. 16 Houston , 42-32, only the third time in Sanders' four seasons that the Buffaloes (4-6) have beaten a ranked team .

"God they were resilient," Sanders said of his players afterward.

They fell behind 20-7 in the second quarter but came storming back to take a 35-20 lead in the third. They also scored their first four touchdowns on big plays by four players — a 38-yard run , a 67-yard run , a 32-yard run and a 53-yard catch.

Then when it was finally over, Colorado fans stormed the field for the second home game in a row , this time at 11:49 p.m. local time on a chilly fall night at Folsom Field in Boulder.

"The way they take the field at the conclusion of the game is like we just won the Super Bowl," Sanders said of the fans. "I'm proud of them. I'm happy because kids love kids. Kids are on the field playing. Kids are in the stands supporting... And kids love kids, regardless of what some may write, what someone may tweet, post or say on your wonderful news stations."

No questions about Deion Sanders' job security after game

Unlike last week, when the Buffs lost at Arizona State , the win quieted questions about Sanders' job security and kept his postseason bowl hopes alive with two winnable games up next at Cincinnati on Nov. 21. and at home against Central Florida on Nov. 28. If they win both, they'd be bowl-eligible with a 6-6 record after starting the season 2-5.

The victory also was Colorado's first against an AP poll Top-15 team since 2007 ( Houston was No. 14 in AP poll).

Afterward, Sanders said he was "really, really thankful that the young fan base don't listen to the foolishness."

He was apparently referencing online criticism of his team's downward trend before Friday.

Colorado's young supporters "don't go online and go back and forth with an idiot that has never been in the stadium," Sanders said.

Colorado safety Randon Fontenette also referenced the outside noise about Sanders before Friday.

"Just coming to the game with Coach Prime, like, you know. we all want him here," Fontenette said. "Like, I came here for him, to play for him. That's why I really play hard, because I love playing for Coach Prime, man. He's a good guy, a good coach, and he's taught me a lot."

How Deion Sanders and Colorado beat Houston

Colorado's Go-Go offense under offensive coordinator Brennan Marion finally came alive as Colorado scored at least 30 points against a Power Four conference team for the first time since 2024. The Buffaloes had five rushing touchdowns and 249 rushing yards on 39 carries, led by Alabama transfer Richard Young , who had 99 yards and two touchdowns.

Colorado's backup quarterback even made a cameo appearance in this run parade. After starting quarterback Isaac Wilson was temporarily knocked out of the game with a left leg injury, his replacement, freshman Kaneal Sweetwyne , then added 14-yard touchdown run on his first play to help put the Buffs up 35-20 with 5:26 left in the third quarter.

"We all caught the same bus," Sanders said — a reference to his offense, defense and special teams coming together this time instead of one or more of them collapsing.

By the time the ride was over, Colorado receiver Joseph Williams found himself surrounded by Colorado fans on the field after the game. His 53-yard touchdown catch early in the third quarter helped Colorado take a 28-20 lead.

"It looked like it was just me out here with 30,000 fans," Williams said. "No, but it was super dope. Our fans always show up, show out for us."

'Everybody's counting us out,' Colorado player says

After Sweetwyne's touchdown, Houston still had more than 20 minutes to catch up. But Colorado hung on and added a 75-yard touchdown drive in the fourth quarter — a possession that ate 6:01 off the clock and gave Colorado a 42-26 lead with 3:59 left.

Houston (7-3) answered with its own 75-yard touchdown drive to cut the lead to the final score with 1:51 left but didn't recover the ensuing onside kick.

Wilson returned to the game after his injury and finished with 17-of-25 passing for 217 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Houston quarterback Conner Weigman completed 26 of 42 passes for 272 yards and three touchdowns with one interception.

"Everybody's counting us out," Williams said. "They say we can't win three games in a row to make a bowl game. But why can't we? Why can't we?"

Deion Sanders says he still expects a lot more

Colorado led 21-20 at halftime after falling behind 20-7 with 2:36 left in the second quarter. Houston had scored two touchdowns and two field goals on its first four possessions. But Colorado got three big plays from three different running backs to score all of its first-half touchdowns in the second quarter, including two in the final two minutes before halftime.

▶ Alabama transfer Richard Young scored the first one — a 38-yarder to help cut Houston's lead to 10-7 with 9:25 left in the second quarter.

▶ Then DeKalon Taylor took a pitch from quarterback Isaac Wilson and ran it in for a 67-yard touchdown with 1:49 before halftime.

▶ After forcing Houston to punt for the first time all game on the next series, Colorado scored again on a 32-yard touchdown run from JaQuail Smith 15 seconds in the half.

It was quite the awakening in front of 47,495 at Folsom Field. Colorado only ran five plays in the first quarter for 13 yards. In the second quarter, Colorado ran 20 plays for 225 yards, including 165 from runs.

"I still expect a lot more from us," Sanders said. "We did some things that we showed you they were capable of doing. We've been capable of this all season long, but we just hadn't put it together. So I'm really proud of the young men that they put it together, as well as the (coaching) staff."

Follow reporter Brent Schrotenboer @Schrotenboer . Email: bschrotenb@usatoday.com

articles.title: Josh Allen vs Patrick Mahomes: The 2026 NFL numbers reveal how the Bills star is challenging the Chiefs quarterback
articles.summary: Ten yards. That is all that separates Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen in passing this season, 2,037 to 2,027, after Week 9.
articles.body: Ten yards. That is all that separates Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen in passing this season, 2,037 to 2,027, after Week 9. Buffalo is 7-1 and Kansas City is 6-2. Allen has scored 21 touchdowns, nine of them rushing. Mahomes has also thrown two fewer interceptions, four to six, but he is dealing with an elbow injury ahead of Sunday's game at Atlanta. The Chiefs visit Buffalo on Nov. 26, and the early numbers suggest Allen is no longer chasing Mahomes. He is level with him, and in some areas ahead.Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes are almost even as passersThe passing numbers are close enough to look like a typo. Mahomes completes 67.3 percent of his throws and Allen 66.1. Spread over eight games, that is about 253 yards a game for Allen and 255 for Mahomes. Before the season, ESPN's Sam Block ranked Mahomes ahead of Allen, while a poll of coaches and executives reported by Outkick leaned the other way. Eight games in, neither camp has a clean win.Allen separates himself on the ground. He has 285 rushing yards to Mahomes' 85.That running also explains the touchdown gap. Allen has 12 touchdown passes and nine rushing scores. Yahoo's tracker lists Mahomes at 15.The team results lean Allen's way. Buffalo averages 32 points a game, Kansas City about 25, and the Chiefs' three-point night in Seattle drags that figure down hard. Without it, they are at 28.Form is the other thing to watch. Mahomes has been sharper lately, throwing for 563 yards and five touchdowns in his last two games, against Denver and the Jets. He completed 73.6 percent of his passes and posted a passer rating of 119.2 over that stretch. Allen's last outing was quieter. He went 21 of 31 for 234 yards with one touchdown and one interception in a 23-6 win at Minnesota, against a defense Yahoo called arguably the league's best.Mahomes' elbow adds a wrinkle before the Nov. 26 gameMahomes hurt his elbow in last week's win over the Jets, then came back into the game. He was listed as questionable for Atlanta earlier this week. The Chiefs also added receiver Josh Downs this week.Kansas City's two losses were ugly. Seattle held the Chiefs to three points on Oct. 25. Denver won 28-24 a week later.Buffalo's lone defeat was a 29-26 home loss to New England on Oct. 4. Allen also carries last January with him, when four turnovers hurt him in a divisional loss to Denver. articles.title: Week 10 Fantasy Injury Report and Last Minute Waiver Wire Replacements
articles.summary: Injuries can be the bane of even the best fantasy drafters. We've seen several stars go down this season, and we saw a couple of significant injuries in Week 9.
articles.body:
Injuries can be the bane of even the best fantasy drafters. We've seen several stars go down this season, and we saw a couple of significant injuries in Week 9.

Los Angeles Rams star Puka Nacua is headed to injured reserve with a neck injury. Arizona Cardinals standout Michael Wilson is done for the year with a neck injury.

While not every injured star is set to miss significant time, the Week 10 injury list extends beyond those two.

Here, we'll dive into the Week 10 injury report , provide rankings for the top remaining point-per-reception (PPR) plays, and highlight sleepers who may still be available on the waiver wire entering the weekend.

There are no big injury surprises at quarterback. Kyler Murray and Sam Darnold are both out this week. Presumably, recent addition Kirk Cousins will start for the Minnesota Vikings, while Drew Lock will start for the Seattle Seahawks

New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith had a rough day against the Kansas City Chiefs last week, finishing with just 7.4 fantasy points. However, he should bounce back this week against the Buffalo Bills.

Buffalo has surrendered an average of 16.8 fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks this season. Its defense looked terrific against the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night, but quarterback play has been a massive issue for Minnesota all year.

The Jets are also hopeful that they'll have receiver Garrett Wilson back this week after he missed Week 9 with a concussion.

Smith reached 19 fantasy points in each of his previous two games before facing Kansas City, and he's rostered in only 23 percent of fantasy leagues.

Aaron Rodgers and Deshaun Watson are also viable sleeper options for Week 10.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Officially, New England Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson is questionable, though ESPN's Adam Schefter reported early in the week that he could be sidelined for a "short period of time."

TreVeyon Henderson is out, along with Josh Jacobs. Kenneth Walker III, Travis Etienne Jr., David Montgomery, and Tyjae Spears are listed as questionable.

New Orleans Saints running back Audric Estimé is a prime waiver target this week, and not just because he's coming off a stellar game.

Estimé did rack up 14.7 fantasy points against the Cleveland Browns last Sunday. That's part of the equation. However, he's also likely to see a prominent role moving forward, as the Saints struggled to run the ball regularly before his return. Furthermore, New Orleans is about to face a Carolina Panthers defense that leads the league in fantasy points surrendered to opposing RBs.

Estimé is still only rostered in 47 percent of fantasy leagues.

Emmett Johnson, Kaelon Black, Dylan Sampson, and Mike Washington Jr. are other running backs to consider scooping up this week.

Marvin Harrison Jr., Carnell Tate, Jauan Jennings, and Mike Evans are the most notable receivers who have been ruled out.

A.J. Brown, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Denzel Boston, Jordan Addison, Skyy Moore, Xavier Legette, Omar Cooper Jr., Adonai Mitchell, Garrett Wilson, and Dont'e Thornton Jr. are listed as questionable.

Chris Bell and Andre Iosivas are doubtful.

Brown is still dealing with a knee injury, which makes DeMario Douglas a solid sleeper option for Week 10. He has topped 15 fantasy points in back-to-back weeks and will likely be relied upon heavily this week against the Detroit Lions.

The Lions have been good against the run and not so good against the pass this season. The Patriots, meanwhile, will be without TreVeyon Henderson and Rhamondre Stevenson, which should lead to a very pass-oriented approach this week.

Expect New England's game plan to revolve around Drake Maye's arm, which bodes well for Douglas and the Patriots' other healthy pass-catchers.

Detroit has surrendered the ninth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers this season. Douglas is still available in over half of fantasy leagues.

Tank Dell, Ryan Flournoy, Pat Bryant, and Konata Mumpfield are other wide receivers worth considering this week.

Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson has been ruled out with wrist and chest injuries. Terrance Ferguson, Jake Ferguson, and Mo Alie-Cox are also out.

Rams tight end Tyler Higbee hasn't reached double-digit fantasy points since 5. However, the Rams may turn to him frequently in the coming weeks with both Nacua and Davante Adams sidelined and Ferguson out.

While Higbee only caught one pass last week, he was targeted five times. He should see an even bigger target share this week, and he has a favorable matchup against Arizona.

The Cardinals have surrendered the eighth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends in 2026. Higbee is rostered in only 13 percent of fantasy leagues.

Darren Waller, Pat Freiermuth, and Darnell Washington are other tight ends to consider this week.

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: "It's a very painful disease": Travis Kelce's mom Donna Kelce shares heartbreaking reason behind her health advocacy while supporting Brooke Shields
articles.summary: Donna Kelce has spent years cheering for her sons, Travis and Jason, through some of the biggest moments of their football careers.
articles.body: Donna Kelce has spent years cheering for her sons, Travis and Jason, through some of the biggest moments of their football careers. But away from the stadium, the NFL mom has also been paying attention to something far more personal: the health of people around her. In January 2025, Donna joined actress Brooke Shields for a health awareness event in Kansas City, where she shared an emotional account of watching friends struggle with shingles. Her words carried a message about pain, missed moments and the importance of taking care of one's health before it is too late.Donna Kelce shared emotional account of friends suffering from shinglesOn January 18, 2025, Donna Kelce hosted a VIP brunch in Kansas City as part of GSK's THRIVE@50+ campaign. The initiative encourages adults aged 50 and older to understand their risk of shingles and discuss prevention with healthcare professionals. Brooke Shields, Gina Torres and Roselyn Sanchez also took part in the awareness effort.The event took place ahead of the Kansas City Chiefs' playoff game against the Houston Texans. However, the conversation moved beyond football when Donna discussed how the condition had affected people close to her.Speaking with Brooke, Donna Kelce recalled seeing friends deal with the painful illness. Her comments offered a glimpse into why she wanted to support the campaign.“I've had a few friends that have developed shingles. It's a very painful disease. You miss out on the most precious moments in your life because you cannot be the person you want to be because you're in pain. If you do get this particular disease, it's not an easy one.”Her words highlighted an often overlooked part of illness. Pain does not only affect the person experiencing it. It can also take away opportunities to spend time with family, attend celebrations and enjoy everyday experiences.Donna did not say that she had personally suffered from shingles. Instead, she spoke about witnessing its effects on her friends.Donna Kelce urged people to take responsibility for their healthDonna's message did not stop with sharing her friends' experiences. She also used the campaign to encourage people to become more aware of their health, particularly as they grow older.In an interview shared by the campaign, she stressed the importance of making personal well-being a priority.“Everybody needs to take ownership of their health, regardless of age. That's the most important thing you can do.”She also offered practical advice to people concerned about shingles, saying:“Ask your doctor or pharmacist about your risk for shingles and about prevention.”Donna had another personal reason for taking part in the campaign. During her appearance, she explained how staying healthy helps her remain present for her family.“One of the most important things that I do to be there for my sons is prioritize my health so I can be here to support them in everything they do. It’s the most important time of the year, playoff season,” Donna said. “And you know me, I’ll never miss a chance to support my boys.”Her comments appeared in a January 19, 2025, report by Us Weekly, following the Chiefs' playoff appearance.The campaign itself had been announced on September 16, 2024, when GSK revealed its partnership with Brooke Shields. Donna was among the women featured in the initiative, which aimed to encourage conversations about healthy ageing and shingles prevention.On March 20, 2025, The Times of India revisited Donna's comments, highlighting her emotional account of watching friends experience the condition.For Donna, the message was not about football victories or public attention. It was about protecting the ability to enjoy life's important moments. Her experience watching friends struggle with pain gave her a reason to speak up, while her role as a mother offered another reminder of why good health matters.She has spent much of her life showing up for Jason and Travis. Now, she is encouraging others to look after themselves so they can keep showing up for the people they love.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
