articles.title: Which NFL Coordinators Should be NFL's Next Top Head Coach Candidates?
articles.summary: The amount of turnover seen among NFL head coaches over the last few seasons has been staggering. The pace won't slow down anytime soon, because professional football is a bottom-line business.
articles.body:
The amount of turnover seen among NFL head coaches over the last few seasons has been staggering. The pace won't slow down anytime soon, because professional football is a bottom-line business.

Jerry Glanville made the now-iconic observation that N.F.L. actually stands for "not for long." He didn't even realize how true his words were, and they've only grown more insightful as the decades pass.

Glanville was referring to poor officiating at the time, but his words turned into a blanket statement that directly applies to coaching. Just over the last three seasons, 25 different head coaching hires have been made. Only seven of the league's current head coaches have been with their team longer than five seasons.

The turnover is astronomical, which finding quality candidates more difficult, especially when the vast majority of hires comes from the NFL ranks.

Let's set aside proven head coaches such as Mike Tomlin, Sear McDermott or even Bruce Arians, who aren't currently on a sideline but may reenter the field. The NFL still hasn't bought into collegiate coaches being able to make a smooth transition.

Instead, five names should be at or near the top of the list once the regular season is complete for those 13 franchises currently with three or fewer wins.

To quote an iconic phrase from the great philosopher Cody Rhodes, the Minnesota Vikings' Brian Flores has gone from " undesirable to un-g**d***-deniable ."

Flores is only candidate on this short list with previous head coaching experience. That experience didn't end well, to the point where Flores and his representation brought a lawsuit against the NFL for alleged racial discrimination in hiring practices. The case remains open, with a federal judge ruling against the NFL in July to turn the matter over to arbitration.

Despite the ongoing litigation, Flores' performance as the Vikings' defensive coordinator has been too good not to be considered for another head coach position, even after finishing with a 24-25 record during his three seasons at the helm of the Miami Dolphins. Currently, Flores' unit is terrorizing the league with the coordinator's carefree attitude toward blitzing on a nearly every-down basis.

Currently, the Vikings rank second in total and pass defense. The figure could be even better if Minnesota had a complementary offense capable of taking some pressure off the other side of the ball. Flores' group finished third in total defense a season ago.

"You try to have answers for everything," Chicago Bears head coach/offensvie play-caller Brian Johnson told ESPN's Courtney Cronin . "He's been in this division three years now, and yeah, I mean you'd like to think he's put everything he could possibly do on tape until you play him next and you realize he hasn't yet. So it'll be something new. There always is with him and that's what makes him such a good coordinator.

"It's a great challenge. It really is. You have a lot of fun on game day. Now the week of preparation is not so much fun, but you know, there's a lot of back and forth that goes into it." The respect for Flores from opposing players and coaches is obvious. He's arguably the game's premier defensive mind. He brings legitimate head coaching experience, too. His unit's performance has others around the league just shaking their heads. All of this should equate to becoming a head coach again in 2027, as long as league owners can get past themselves.

Today's NFL is typically looking for the next great offensive play-caller to lead a franchise since it's a quarterback-driven league. Those top play-callers have been hired over the last few years.

Thus, a candidate like Grant Udinski becomes a desirable candidate even though he isn't the Jacksonville Jaguars' play-caller, because he's only 30 yards old, with working experience with two games the game's best offensive minds in Liam Coen and Kevin O'Connell.

"He's so unbelievably gifted in his ability to look at the game, study the game and then articulate it with not only his ideas, his imagination, but then how do we get those thoughts to the players to be able to take advantage of those things," O'Connell told Danielle Lerner of USA Today . "His future's so bright and we're probably all going to be working for him eventually. It's just a matter of time."

Every NFL team wants the next Sean McVay, who took over the Los Angeles Rams at the ripe age of 31 thanks to his offensive wizardry. He's now a Super Bowl-winning head coach. Every organization is looking for the next great mind and each tends to look in the same areas. Both O'Connell and Coen both worked for McVay at one time. Now, Udinski is helping orchestrate the league's fourth-ranked scoring offense. He and Coen have helped unlock Trevor Lawrence's potential and gotten the most out of the 2021 No. 1 overall draft pick. Despite not calling plays in Jacksonville, all of these factors are important when placing Udinski atop the list among the offensive-minded candidates.

If there's one thing NFL owners love, they are often smitten by young offensive minds with a pedigree. Technically, that's three different qualifiers. But they're all wrapped up into one with the San Francisco 49ers' Klay Kubiak. Two coaching trees currently dominate the league. Sean McVay's influence, as mentioned earlier, has developed into an weeping willow with how far his branches cascade over today's NFL. The Kyle Shanahan pipeline serves as the other. These two approaches aren't diametrically opposed, either, as it used to be when teams would choose between Bill Walsh- or Don Coryell-inspired candidates. In this instance, significant overlap exists between McVay and Shanahan. When it comes to the younger Kubiak, who older brother was named the Las Vegas Raiders' head coach earlier this year, the 38-year-old works directly with Shanahan and currently serves as the Niners' offensive coordinator. Unlike his brother, Kubiak has not been a primary NFL play-caller. Shanahan retains those duties in San Francisco. However, the immersion in what's often referred to as the NFL's best offensive scheme certainly should have some influence on the coach Kubiak will become if he gets an opportunity to lead his own team. What's fascinating about the 49ers' offensive success is that it maintains even when the roster is best by injuries. The scheme helps to overcome, which is vital in a 100-percent injury league. The approach will help any coach. Plus, football is in Kubiak's blood, as the son of former Houston Texans and Denver Broncos head coach Gary Kubiak. His family's history and ties throughout the league should run deep and help the candidate eventually gather a competent coaching staff.

Aden Durde would be an inspiring choice as an NFL head coach based on his rise to the position. He's also deserving of strong consideration based on his work during recent seasons.

Durde was born in Middlesex, England. He picked up American football at the prep level before attending North Iowa Area Community College. From there, Durde earned playing opportunities at NFL Europe before a practice squad stints with the Carolina Panthers and Kansas City Chiefs.

The linebacker-turned-coach took advantage of the NFL fellowship program and even served as the league's head of football development at NFLUK for three years. He was eventually hired by the Atlanta Falcons and worked his way up from defensive quality coach to Dallas Cowboys defensive line coach to the Seattle Seahawks' defensive coordinator. In doing so, he became the league's first full-time British-born coach.

"I didn't have a career path," Durde told The Seattle Times ' Bob Condotta . "There wasn't like, 'Oh, I'm going to be an accountant or I'm going to do this or that.' That wasn't how I lived my life. I just had this one thing that I absolutely loved."

Granted, Mike Macdonald is Seattle's defensive play-caller. Although, Macdonald relinquished the responsibility during this year's training camp and the start of preseason, allowing his coordinator to gain critical experience. Still, Durde's influence over the game's top-ranked defense shouldn't be overlooked.

"He has a huge role in our stunts and our games and the way that we pass rush," defensive lineman Leonard Williams said. "People have been talking all year about how good of a job we do to get to the quarterback with just four down linemen and I think AD is the one controlling all of that." Durde is the coordinator of an elite, Super Bowl-winning unit. He more than deserves to draw serious interest during the next hiring cycle and complete his incredible, albeit unlikely, journey.

Legacy and experience working alongside Sean McVay are two feathers in the cap of Los Angeles Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula.

Name recognition goes a long way in the NFL. The Rams' defensive play-caller is the grandson of Hall of Fame coach Don Shula and former Cincinnati Bengals head coach Dave Shula. However, his candidacy isn't rooted in nepotism. Chris Shula has earned consideration as McVay's defensive leader over the last three seasons.

Currently, the Rams field a top-five defense. Usually, offensive candidates are preferred from McVay's staff. In this instance, a defensive mind shouldn't make the 40-year-old Shula a lesser option.

Candidates to be an NFL head coach shouldn't be defined entirely by their specific expertise. Interested franchise should be looking for the right leadership qualities to relate with players, get the most out of them and galvanize a locker room. A head coach essentially serves as a de factor CEO of a billion-dollar organization and requires a big-picture outlook.

"There's a lot of love and experience together going back to even playing ball with him in college," McVay said at the end of last year, per Brock Vierra of Sports Illustrated . "I think there are a lot of consistencies that we can relate to in terms of coming from football families and understanding this space. It's really all those things that I just talked about. He checks all those boxes. I think what's really cool is he's had a chance to coach on all three levels. He and I are so connected in regard to how we see the game and how we believe the game should be played, from an offensive, a defensive and really just a holistic perspective."

McVay continued, "Chris will be the first to tell you, 'This is a collective effort.' You hear the headsets on game day and what a phenomenal job he and our defensive coaches do of collaborating to try to be able to put our guys in good positions throughout the game and having a feel for all what's needed. 'How do we want to play that? What's their approach?' He's a stud."

articles.title: New Lamar Jackson Rumors Update When Ravens QB Had Surgery amid Latest Injury Timeline for Return
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens star quarterback Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this season based on when he had thumb surgery.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens star quarterback Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this season based on when he had thumb surgery.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , Jackson's surgery happened last week so based on the estimated recovery time of six to 10 weeks, he could potentially be back on the field before the regular season ends.

Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said in a statement on Nov. 13 that Jackson's recovery timeline was "challenging to predict" after he underwent surgery to address a dislocated and broken right thumb.

"He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return," Minter said. "We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season."

A six-week recovery would have Jackson back around Week 15 when the Ravens play the Pittsburgh Steelers. The full 10-week timeline would give him a chance to play in Week 18, also against the Steelers.

In addition to his hand injury, Jackson also missed three games earlier in the year after suffering a high ankle sprain. In five games, he played just 14 full quarters and threw for 961 yards, six touchdowns and one interception while adding 144 rushing yards and another score.

In the wake of Jackson's injury, the Ravens traded for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who is expected to make his first start for the team against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football in Week 10. At 4-5, Baltimore has work to do if it hopes to make the playoffs.

The Ravens will likely remain cautious with Jackson's recovery, making the acquisition of Brissett a critical move as they look to snap their four-game losing streak going into Monday night.

articles.title: Dolphins Predicted to Replace Malik Willis With ‘Gunslinger’ Quarterback
articles.summary: On Sunday, the Miami Dolphins will not start Malik Willis at quarterback. Willis suffered a groin injury prior to Miami’s game against the New England Patrio...
articles.body:
On Sunday, the Miami Dolphins will not start Malik Willis at quarterback. Willis suffered a groin injury prior to Miami's game against the New England Patriots. While Willis then started two games for the Dolphins, the quarterback's rushing ability was significantly impacted by his groin injury.

Following Miami's game against the Lions, the Dolphins placed Willis on injured reserve, which will keep him out for at least four games. Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said that Willis will be the team's starting quarterback when he returns. However, despite that statement, Willis' play has not secured his position as the team's franchise quarterback going into the future.

For that reason, the Dolphins have been predicted to select a quarterback in Bleacher Report's latest mock draft.

Miami Dolphins Predicted to Add Gunslinger Quarterback

Bleacher Report's Brent Sobleski released his latest mock draft, which includes the Miami Dolphins drafting Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker with the third overall pick. Sobleski wrote of the team fit: "Malik Willis is well on his way to becoming a one-and-done starting NFL quarterback. To be fair, the Miami Dolphins surrounded their current QB1 with very little talent, which has only made Willis' life more difficult. Even so, the Dolphins can't pass on an opportunity to select the 2027 class' top quarterback prospect."

Regarding the scouts' perspective on Mestemaker, Sobleski wrote: "Drew Mestemaker has the size, mobility and arm talent to be a playmaking threat at the next level. His big arm allows him to throw the ball deep and generate velocity to zip passes into tight windows. He brings a gunslinger mentality, but his decision-making will only improve as the game slows down. Mestemaker will enter the NFL with a high ceiling and solid floor."

In eight games this season, Willis has completed 58% of his passes for 1,396 passing yards, six passing touchdowns and six interceptions. On the ground, Willis has added 232 rushing yards and three touchdowns. If he returns after four weeks, Willis will have five more games to prove why he should be the team's quarterback moving forward.

If the Dolphins do decide to add a quarterback in the 2027 NFL Draft, Mestemaker would probably be at the top of the list. He's currently the second-ranked prospect by ESPN's Mel Kiper, behind only wide receiver Jeremiah Smith.

Regarding Mestemaker, Kiper wrote: "Mestemaker didn't even start at quarterback for his high school team; he was the punter, played some safety and was the backup QB. Then he walked on at North Texas in 2024 as a QB before becoming the starter in 2025. After throwing for more than 4,000 yards, Mestemaker transferred with coach Eric Morris to Oklahoma State. It's an incredible story.

His toolbox is also pretty incredible. I love the way he scans the field and bides his time in the pocket. Mestemaker has the big arm to make all of the throws, with 48 completions going for 20-plus yards this season (most in the FBS). But he also has the mobility to pick up nice chunks of yardage on the ground. Mestemaker shows linebacker-esque toughness and plays with a competitive edge. He doesn't turn 21 years old until January, and he has just 24 career starts to his name. So, there's a lot of untapped potential."

articles.title: Commanders clear mission is to catch the Giants by Week 18 - Daily Slop
articles.summary: If both teams finish with identical records, Washington wins the tie-breaker
articles.body:
Editor's note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy!

The good news is the Commanders now own the tie-breaker advantage with New York, something that could factor into things down the stretch.

By rule, the October tie counts as half a win and half a loss for each team. Head-to-head record is the NFL's first tiebreaker between two clubs in the same division.

If Washington goes 5-3 over its final eight games and New York goes 3-5, both would finish 8-8-1. In a two-team tie, the Commanders would finish ahead of the Giants because they went 1-0-1 against them. Thursday's win gave Washington that edge, but it still has to erase the two-game gap. That example assumes a two-team tie; a three-team tie involving Dallas would follow the NFL's separate tiebreaking procedure.

Make no mistake: Washington still has to stack wins. After the mini-bye, New York hosts Jacksonville on Sunday, November 22, and the Commanders host Cincinnati the following night. A Giants loss and a Washington win would cut the gap to one game. The teams won't meet again this season, so the head-to-head edge only matters if the Commanders make up the ground elsewhere.

To read more of this article, CLICK HERE

[The Isaiah Likely touchdown] was a major breakdown, but it didn't change how Jones operated. He maintained an attacking mindset. It proved instrumental in a 24-21 win over New York that may have saved Washington's season.

"The easy thing would be to be nervous in that spot and to back off," Coach Dan Quinn said. "But he's aggressive."

The previous time these teams met, Jones had a conservative approach on defense. Washington blew a 14-point lead in the fourth quarter and ultimately settled for a tie .

New York ran on its first two plays, forcing Washington to burn a couple of timeouts and setting up a pivotal third and one. The Giants were in an empty formation, but the Commanders had eight players along the line of scrimmage prepared for another blitz. It wound up being a designed run for McCarthy, but a blitzing Styles blew up the play.

"Starting with coach DJ, he has confidence in us," Styles said. "Plays are going to happen. You clean them up. Hopefully, you don't make the same mistakes, but plays are going to happen. The other team, they make money, too.

"But for him to keep that confidence as the game goes on and not pull back, I think it just shows he sees the improvement. He's getting more and more comfortable with the guys he's got out there, in terms of us being able to execute on a consistent basis, especially later in the game."

"Defensively, they were not only keeping us in the game," Quinn said. "I thought they won the game."

Download the SB Nation app Commanders fans, take command of game day!

Follow the action and share every cheer, question and instant reaction with fellow fans on the SB Nation app.

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android .

The calls for Quinn's job won't completely abate unless and until wins are stacked on top of each other, and this is a group that hasn't posted back-to-back victories since the playoffs that followed the 2024 season. It's been a minute.

But what has been reestablished over Washington's past five games — all Daniels starts — is that the quarterback gives them a chance any time they line up, and that it's not impossible for him to stay healthy for long stretches, even entire seasons, at a time. Did you watch Thursday night and obsess over the brace that's keeping Daniels' left elbow in place? Me neither.

When Daniels plays, he can build on his own performances. When he gets hurt — and he did miss two September games with that dislocated left elbow — he's almost starting over, at least at this point in his still-nascent career. In the five games since his return, he has completed 67.3 percent of his throws for 248 yards per game with seven touchdowns and just the two picks. He owns the eighth-best passer rating in the league over that span.

Thursday was enormous for the stability of the entire franchise. It's important that Daniels was at the fulcrum. The winning play didn't come completely from embattled first-year coordinator David Blough. It was third-and-4 from the Giants' 32.

"I gave a little signal to Stef," Daniels said, "and he went on a slant — and the rest is history."

The little signal wasn't by accident. The little signal was developed during the course of the week. Diggs will turn 33 later this month and is in his 12th NFL season. He has seen nearly everything. His impression of Daniels, in that moment, with the season in the balance?

"Baby Kobe," Diggs said, invoking the name of Daniels' athletic hero. "He's gonna be the same kind of player he is in the beginning of the game and at the end of games."

Daniels has played five consecutive games since sitting out two because of a dislocated left elbow. It is the most games he has played in a row since starting all 20 contests in his rookie season. On Thursday, he completed 23 of 33 passes for 249 yards and three touchdowns.

But playing that many games consecutively has helped him find a groove, he said.

"I'm starting to get into that rhythm," Daniels said. "It shows the more games you play consistently, the more reps you get, the more flow in the rhythm that you can [find]. And it was tough last year being in and out of the lineup and trying to catch a rhythm."

Being in a rhythm might have helped Daniels on his final throw. When New York showed a cover zero blitz, Daniels gave a signal to Diggs, who ran a slant against corner Dru Phillips and then broke his tackle attempt and sped to the end zone where he turned at the 1, paused and fell backward into the end zone.

"He'll be the same player he is in the beginning of the game as he is in the end of the game," Diggs said. "Things will happen good and bad and he isn't going to change."

To read more of this ESPN article, CLICK HERE

Against the Giants, the Commanders converted 7-of-14 third downs. Six came with one yard to go, including Sinnott's third-and-goal touchdown. All three of Washington's touchdowns came on third down.

Washington ran the ball 33 times Thursday, gaining 105 yards. Daniels accounted for 11 attempts and 28 yards, and the offense still went 0-for-2 on fourth down. That's a lot to clean up for a team that needed all three touchdowns to beat New York. Cincinnati is coming to town November 23, giving Quinn and offensive coordinator David Blough 11 days to build on what worked. Their next test is whether Washington can still move the chains on third down when it needs more than four yards.

Part of the reason Daniels was so efficient for most of the night was because of how well his offensive line protected him. The Giants had the third-highest blitz rate in the league heading into Thursday's game, and they brought plenty of it to try and hamper Daniels.

Daniels, however, felt little of it all night. He was only sacked one time, and he was only pressured on 17.9% of his dropbacks — the second-lowest of his career.

"Let's give some love to the big uglies up front," Willie Colon said on "Good Morning Football."

The Giants have become one of the league's better defenses, ranking fifth in yards allowed and 11th in third-down efficiency. The Commanders did not have their best offensive night with 340 yards, but the unit functioned well when it needed to do so. The offense had 105 total yards on the ground and committed only four penalties all night. Nick Allegretti, who stepped in at center for Lucas Patrick, did a good job of leading the offensive front, and the group only allowed four pressures.

There is still work to be done up front, but give credit where it's due: the offensive line stepped up to the challenge in front of them.

Giants kicker Dominic Zvada appeared to get off a quality kickoff, with the ball bouncing in the landing zone at the 11-yard line and staying in bounds.

However, the Giants were penalized for a kickoff out of bounds, and the Commanders' offense started the drive at the 40-yard line.

The reason is that McCaffrey willfully went out of bounds, kept his feet planted and lunged forward to corral the ball, which settled just inside the yard-line markers. According to Rule 3, Section 20, Article 1 and Article 3, the ball was considered out of bounds, even though it never crossed the boundary.

Article 1 states: "A player or an official is out of bounds when he touches a boundary line, or when he touches anything that is on or outside a boundary line, except a player, an official, or a pylon."

By this definition, McCaffrey was clearly out of bounds. That takes it to Article 3, Item 2: Loose Ball.

"A loose ball that is not in player control is out of bounds when it touches a boundary line or anything that is on or outside such line, including a player, an official, or a pylon," the rulebook states.

This isn't the first time this sort of play has happened in the NFL. There have been multiple examples before, including a decade ago when Green Bay Packers wide receiver Ty Montgomery executed the play against the Detroit Lions.

This rule more commonly comes into play when a fumble and a scramble to recover the ball near the sidelines occur. If a player who is out of bounds touches the ball in that scenario, possession doesn't just go to that player's team; the ball is considered dead at the spot because that player is an extension of out of bounds with a loose ball in play.

Similarly, McCaffrey was an extension of being out of bounds Thursday, and it worked out in the Commanders' favor.

Outside of Okonkwo, Washington's tight end group through the first nine weeks of the season hasn't had the production many hoped to see. Head coach Dan Quinn noted in the lead up to this Week 10 game that it was an area they wanted to "continue to elevate higher." A different piece of the Commanders TE room came to life in a way previously not seen through the first three seasons of his career in the win against the Giants.

This was a breakout game for Ben Sinnott. His first involvement was a relatively mundane five-yard pickup not long into the second quarter. In his next bit of action, he collected a short pass down the middle from Daniels and showed off his athleticism, hurdling a Giants defender, on the way to a first down. Just before the half, the #82 scored his first touchdown of the season, hauling in a strike from Daniels through traffic. He finished the game with 42 yards on four receptions, the most he has ever had in a single game in his career.

"I got the opportunities tonight," Sinnott said after the game. "I took advantage, and it feels good."

During his All-22 analysis of the contest, Orlovsky focused on the third-down play that eventually resulted in Styles securing a vital tackle for loss on quarterback J.J. McCarthy. And he was astonished by what he found.

Orlovsky pointed to Styles getting everyone in position pre-snap. When he spotted something — probably what the play was going to be — he immediately checked everyone, marshaling proceedings like a seasoned veteran and making sure everyone was in the right position.

Just before the snap, Styles shifts his body to the right, even before McCarthy goes that way. He knew precisely what was coming, and his superb closing speed allowed him to make a critical play with everything on the line.

Speaking to reporters in the locker room, Styles broke down his thought process on the play:

"I was just really thinking about the last time we played 'em. (They had) a 3rd-and-4 situation around like midfield and then ran crack-toss to the back. And then they went empty, (I was) kinda just looking at the tight end and he looked like he was cracking, and I think somebody else, I think Charles (Omenihu) said something too. We kinda had the idea it was QB run, so just wreck it."

By diagnosing the quarterback crack sweep before the snap and shooting through to drop McCarthy for a two-yard loss right before the two-minute warning, Styles forced a Giants punt that set up Washington's game-winning touchdown drive.

Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams Step Up Without Terry McLaurin

With McLaurin out for the season, Washington needs its other receivers to shoulder more responsibility in the passing game. Thursday was an encouraging step in the right direction.

Diggs wasn't just responsible for the game-winning touchdown. He finished with six receptions for 83 yards, leading Washington in both catches and receiving yards.

Meanwhile, rookie wide receiver Antonio Williams continued to show why the organization is excited about his potential. Williams found the end zone in the third quarter for a 31-yard touchdown.

Nick Cross was one of several free-agent signings made this offseason. The move was largely overlooked compared to others, but the Washington Commanders must be thrilled with the impact he's had on the defensive unit so far.

The former Maryland star is a versatile defensive back, and coordinator Daronte Jones is maximizing his potential.

Cross is a violent hitter who thrives closer to the line of scrimmage. His explosiveness on blitzes is exceptional, and he caused significant disruption against the New York Giants, playing an understated yet vital role in the team's overall success.

Just why Cross hesitated when he had a free run on Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy before tight end Isaiah Likely's touchdown is anyone's guess. It doesn't matter now, and aside from that brief moment of doubt, it was another assured performance from the veteran.

The South Alabama product's performance against the New York Giants was arguably his best of the campaign. Reaves was flying around the field with controlled aggression, becoming a linchpin on the back end. This allowed Nick Cross to get closer to the line of scrimmage on blitz packages, providing the balance Jones is looking for.

Reaves finished the game with nine tackles , one pass breakup, and one quarterback hit.

The NFL's Instagram post , a slow-motion video of Hartman running the 40-yard dash at the NFL Combine, racked up over a million views by midday. Static photos posted by the Commanders and ESPN netted more than 400,000 collective likes in the same period.

The long-running reality TV franchise was arguably in need of some football field–sized firepower after the most recent season of its sister show, The Bachelorette, was canceled just three days before its scheduled premiere earlier this year amid domestic abuse allegations against its lead, Taylor Frankie Paul.

Hartman's season will reportedly begin filming in January and premiere on March 21. The Commanders declined to respond to questions from FOS about whether the QB—who is currently fifth on the depth chart—would step away from his duties with the team to participate, or whether the organization will continue to promote his involvement.

The NFL did not immediately respond to questions about its promotional plans. However, the league hasn't been shy about spotlighting players' romantic lives; in August, a source close to the NFL told FOS that viral videos of quarterbacks spending personal time with their significant others while on the field at training camp were part of a coordinated campaign to reach female fans. At the time, the NFL also said it was "scaling up its female-focused content" and would "be doing even more in the future."

Four Key Plays that Led to the Commanders Week 10 Win

With some LeBron James/James Harden-level flopping, Treylon Burks dragged Deonte Banks into a 33-yard pass interference call in the closing minutes. (The Commanders scored the winning points on that possession.)

Meanwhile, the same Giant who had puked on the sideline after eating a pretzel-wrapped hot dog before kickoff froze in his stance as Jameis Winston failed to gain a crucial first down on a quarterback sneak. Harbaugh said Friday that Cam Skattebo, who played a game worthy of the "Iron Man" helmet he wore to the stadium, was not supposed to be shoving Winston from behind because the designed play was not a "tush push."

But why wasn't it a "tush push," given the Giants' success with that play, and why wasn't Skattebo or Patrick Ricard or some other raging bull out there driving Winston across the line?

In the end, this was one of many unforced Giants errors in the narrow divide separating winners from losers.

The Giants probably need to finish at 8-8-1 or 9-7-1 to win the division, meaning they might need to KO one or two of the relative heavyweights on their schedule. And so be it.

The Giants still have the Jacksonville Jaguars and San Francisco 49ers at home and the Seattle Seahawks and Detroit Lions on the road. Games against the Cleveland Browns at home and the Dallas Cowboys are winnable, but certainly not gimmes. The only seemingly uncontested layups left are the Indianapolis Colts on the road and the Philadelphia Eagles at home.

[I]t appears possible…that they could go 0-4 against the Jaguars, 49ers, Seahawks and Lions…. They haven't won at Dallas in a decade, and victories over the Colts, Browns and Eagles alone might not be enough.

So if the Giants fail to make the playoffs, this 24-21 loss will haunt them until opening day of the 2027 season … and beyond.

McCarthy explained his last two throws postgame.

"My thought process was pop it up to my playmakers, have them go make a play," McCarthy said.

That did not sit well with former NFL linebacker Emmanuel Acho.

"This is the problem when you are relying on a young bull like J.J. McCarthy to take you to the promised land," Acho said live on Speakeasy . "It's one thing to make a mistake once. Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on J.J. McCarthy.

"The Commanders ran the exact same play on back-to-back plays. J.J., you got away with the first duck when [Jeremy] Reeves hit you in the arm and they dropped the pick. They run zero again, and you have no plan. Football is all about have a plan, execute the plan…how are you surprised when you see the same play the second time? They just showed it to you."

The Giants (5-3-1) host the AFC South-leading Jaguars (6-2) next Sunday.

New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers on Friday responded to criticism of the idea that he could have given a better effort to knock the ball down on a game-ending interception by Rasul Douglas of the Washington Commanders on Thursday night in the Giants' 24-21 loss.

"Seeing the ball go up at the time, didn't really see him [Douglas] or where he was, so I'm not really aware of that," Nabers said. "My head is looking up at the ball, even though he was driving on the ball. So, just seeing how high the ball was and just waiting for it to come down and made a jump to catch the ball and then got hit and then he made a play."

Nabers and Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels were LSU teammates and remain close friends. Nabers aid it was "bugging me pretty bad" that he has never beaten Daniels as a pro.

"He calls me all the time," Nabers said. "He's probably trying to call me right now, but I can't answer that phone call."

Nabers said he has a hard time letting go of lost games.

"Every loss stings. Every loss I think we go through, it stings and it hurts, but you got to have your own flush mindset," he said.

Nick Sirianni wouldn't rule out coaching changes after the game Sunday, but he did say a day later that no changes have been made.

"Right now, like I said earlier, we're going through our self-scout process," he said. "Guys are working on studies right now and we're determined to figure things out and get on the right track, and that's what we're worried about right this particular time."

That wasn't a ringing endorsement of Mannion staying in his current role. Could the Eagles make a change at play-caller as soon as this week? Could they move on from offensive line coach Chris Kuper? The self-scouting process won't be kind to either coach.

If Mannion remains in his position for the rest of the season, it'll be worth watching if the offense can show signs of life, with Joe Milton or whoever is taking snaps at quarterback.

There's also the Sirianni of it all. Will Jeffrey Lurie and Howie Roseman think injuries and a flawed roster outweigh the rest of the problems and decide to keep him? Is there a number of consecutive losses that warrant an in-season firing?

The 49ers are an extremely tough matchup for the Cowboys

Another thing the 49ers do better than any team in the league this season is limit the opposing team's success on the ground. San Francisco leads the league in defensive rush EPA (-0.215) and Y/A allowed (3.3). The 49ers have not given up 100 rushing yards in a game since their Week 2 matchup against the Miami Dolphins, when they surrendered just 102.

The 49ers have been dominant at stopping the run all season, but their last three games in particular have been as good as it gets in that department. San Francisco has allowed an average of just 53 rushing yards over those three games, along with a remarkable – 0.290 defensive rush EPA and a 34.9% rush SR .

When the Cowboys' offense has lacked balance this season, they've struggled. It's going to be extremely hard for Dallas' offense to play complementary football on Sunday against this San Francisco run defense. If the 49ers continue their trench dominance, it may be a long afternoon for the Cowboys.

articles.title: Bruce Arians says Andrew Luck could do something that even Tom Brady couldn’t
articles.summary: Tom Brady is the undisputed greatest NFL player of all time for many people, but Bruce Arians has admitted that Andrew Luck could do something even Brady cou...
articles.body:
Tom Brady is the undisputed greatest NFL player of all time for many people, but Bruce Arians has admitted that Andrew Luck could do something even Brady couldn't.

Arians had the privilege of working with some of the best quarterbacks to play the game, including his Super Bowl-winning stint with Brady and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He was also able to work alongside the likes of Peyton Manning and Ben Roethlisberger.

Undoubtedly, Arians will recognise that Brady was the best player he ever had the opportunity to work alongside, but there was something about Luck that even the great Tom Brady was unable to match.

Luck lasted seven seasons in the NFL before calling it time on his career. He may not have had the longevity of someone like Brady or Roethlisberger, but his photographic memory is something that Arians cannot forget.

Bruce Arians reveals what Andrew Luck had that even Tom Brady did not possess

Albeit a very short career, Luck enjoyed an outstanding stint in the NFL, which returned four Pro Bowls and the 2018 NFL Comeback Player of the Year award, among many other titles. His time with the Colts clearly left a lasting impression on Arians.

"Andrew was like, 'I got it, let's roll.' Andrew Luck had a photographic memory because he didn't take any notes. Peyton had notebook upon notebook… Tom had notebook on top of notebook. And I'm looking at Andrew and said, 'You don't need to take any notes?' 'Because I got it.' 'No, you don't.' And he would literally spit it back verbatim," Arians told Jordan Schultz.

I always tell the story about Andrew. Chuck Pagano did a great job of situational football, and I think we were getting ready to play Jacksonville. The week before, the Vikings had just scored: there's 28 seconds left, they had two timeouts, what are you going to do to win the game? So we put our scenario in, and lo and behold, the exact scenario happens in our game that Sunday.

"Andrew's not even waiting for me, he's already on the field: 'I got it, I got it, we walked through this twice.' He completes the pass, calls timeout. Completes the pass, calls timeout. Boom, kick field goal, win the game."

Luck may not have ended his career with the same accolades as someone like Brady, but it is apparent that he had a rare talent that very few quarterbacks in the history of the NFL would be able to come close to.

Unfortunately for Luck, his short career ended without a Super Bowl to his name, which is something the likes of Brady, Manning and Roethlisberger will always have over the 37-year-old.

articles.title: NFL Announces Emergency Officiating Changes Ahead of Week 10 Games
articles.summary: The NFL announces emergency officiating changes for Week 10 due to nationwide flight disruptions. Here's what it means for the Detroit Lions.
articles.body:
The NFL is being forced to make some unusual last-minute adjustments ahead of Sunday's Week 10 games. And this time, it has nothing to do with player injuries, weather conditions, or questionable coaching decisions.

According to ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter , the league has announced changes to its officiating assignments because of the nationwide air travel disruptions that began Friday.

The situation has become serious enough that three backup referees will be called upon to serve as lead officials for multiple games this weekend.

NFL Makes Emergency Changes to Officiating Crews

In a statement shared by Schefter on X , the NFL explained its decision to reassign officials.

"Due to the ongoing nationwide impact to air travel this weekend, the NFL has adjusted its officiating assignments for Week 10 games, reassigning officials to games within driving distance of their hometowns."

According to the league, the adjustments will require three officials who normally serve in other positions to step into the referee role.

Carolina Panthers vs. New Orleans Saints: Duane Heydt

Jacksonville Jaguars vs. Tennessee Titans: Barry Anderson

Miami Dolphins vs. Indianapolis Colts: Don Willard

Pittsburgh Steelers vs. Cincinnati Bengals: Don Willard

The NFL also explained that all 17 officiating crews have a designated backup referee who trains throughout the season to take over if necessary. That preparation is now being put to the test under circumstances that nobody could have anticipated heading into the weekend.

What Does This Mean for the Detroit Lions?

The Detroit Lions are preparing for their Week 10 showdown against the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. Fortunately, the NFL's announcement does not identify the Lions' game as one of the contests requiring an emergency referee assignment.

Detroit and New England are already in Germany preparing for Sunday's game, which is scheduled to kick off at 9:30 a.m. ET. The Lions are looking to extend their four-game winning streak, and Dan Campbell has expressed confidence in his team's preparation for the international matchup.

The NFL's decision is another reminder of just how much Friday's air travel problems have disrupted the sports world. And while the league appears to have contingency plans in place, having to shuffle officials around the country less than 24 hours before Sunday's slate of games is certainly not something you see every week.

articles.title: John Harbaugh faces Stephen A. Smith’s brutal criticism as Giants’ late collapse raises fresh questions about his coaching
articles.summary: Stephen A.
articles.body: Stephen A. Smith has strongly criticised New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh after his team suffered a painful 24-21 defeat against the Washington Commanders on Thursday Night Football. Smith was particularly unhappy with the Giants’ decisions in the final minutes, accusing Harbaugh of playing too cautiously when his team had a chance to secure the win. He also connected the defeat to problems from Harbaugh’s Baltimore days.Stephen A. Smith calls out John Harbaugh for coaching scared in Giants’ lossSpeaking on ESPN’s First Take on Friday, November 13, Smith did not hold back while discussing Harbaugh’s decisions against Washington. He felt the Giants had done enough to put themselves in a winning position but failed to finish the job because their coaching became too defensive.“They were coaching scared. I mean, John Harbaugh should be ashamed of himself. The point that I’m making is this. John Harbaugh, this is not new. This is one of the problems that existed in Baltimore in terms of being outdated.”Smith’s criticism came after the Giants struggled to make progress with the ball despite receiving two major chances to put the game away. New York had taken a 21-17 lead with 8:13 remaining when quarterback J.J. McCarthy connected with tight end Isaiah Likely for a 66-yard touchdown.Things then looked even better for the Giants as safety Jevon Holland intercepted Jayden Daniels, followed by another interception from Ar’Darius Washington on Washington’s next possession. However, New York’s offense failed to take advantage of either turnover.The Giants recorded only 31 net yards across their final three possessions, giving the Commanders enough time to fight back. Washington took possession with 1:47 remaining and needed just three plays to cover 71 yards. Daniels then found Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left, putting the Commanders ahead 24-21.McCarthy’s interception with 25 seconds remaining ended New York’s final attempt to recover.Smith also brought up Jameis Winston’s unusual “Who Let the Dogs Out” cadence, which became another talking point from the game. Winston used the call on fourth-and-inches from the Giants’ 11-yard line in an attempt to draw Washington offside. However, the attempt failed, and New York eventually had to punt.John Harbaugh’s fourth-quarter problems in Baltimore return to the spotlightFor Smith, the defeat was not just about one bad night in New York. He believes Harbaugh has shown similar problems before, particularly when his teams have to protect a lead late in a game.There is a statistic that adds weight to this criticism. According to DraftKings, Harbaugh has now lost 47 games after holding a fourth-quarter lead since becoming Baltimore Ravens head coach in 2008. That is the highest number for any NFL head coach during that period. NFL Research had recorded 46 such losses through the 2025 season, placing him second on the list at that time. Thursday’s defeat added another one.His Baltimore record, however, tells a much bigger story. Harbaugh spent 18 seasons with the Ravens, finishing with a 180-113 regular-season record. He also guided the team to 12 playoff appearances and won Super Bowl XLVII. His success in Baltimore is not in question, but his teams’ struggles to protect leads have continued to attract attention.The reaction to Thursday’s game was not limited to Smith. Sports commentator Bill Simmons also criticised the Giants coach, writing on social media, “Incredible job by John Harbaugh figuring out how to get out coached by Dan Quinn.” Rapper Freddie Gibbs shared his frustration as well, writing, “I don’t wanna hear no more John Harbaugh coach of the year talk.”Harbaugh, meanwhile, did not agree that the loss pointed to a bigger problem with his coaching. He described the result as disappointing and said the team could not allow one defeat to affect its confidence.Despite the setback, New York remains at the top of the NFC East with a 5-3-1 record. Washington is now 3-5-1 and holds the tiebreaker after Thursday’s win and the teams’ earlier tie. The Giants will next host the Jacksonville Jaguars on November 22, giving Harbaugh and his players another chance to respond.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: New Eagles Trade Rumors Reveal Dallas Goedert Eyed by NFC Rival at 2026 NFL Deadline
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles received inquiries from several teams about trading tight end Dallas Goedert, ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported on Saturday.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles received inquiries from several teams about trading tight end Dallas Goedert, ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported on Saturday.

Among those teams were the San Francisco 49ers, but ultimately, Philadelphia elected to keep the 31-year-old tight end on the roster, and he "never got close to being traded," according to Schefter and Rapoport.

The Eagles signed Goedert to a one-year, $7 million contract extension in March to keep him in Philadelphia for the 2026 season, per Spotrac . He could sign another extension that would keep him on the team through 2027, according to Schefter and Rapoport.

Amid a disappointing campaign, the Eagles elected to trade defensive tackle Jordan Davis and center Cam Jurgens ahead of the NFL trade deadline last Tuesday. Despite those moves, the front office evidently felt that Goedert was more valuable than whatever draft compensation they could receive for him.

Goedert was selected with the No. 49 overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft, and he has spent the entirety of his eight-year career in Philadelphia. He had limited opportunities early in his career as he sat behind three-time Pro Bowl tight end Zach Ertz, but Goedert's development allowed Eagles general manager Howie Roseman to trade Ertz to the Arizona Cardinals in 2021.

Although the Eagles have several young tight ends on their roster, none of them have shown the ability to replace Goedert's production.

The Eagles started the 2026 season with two close wins, but they are entering their Week 10 bye with a 2-7 record after losing seven consecutive games. With quarterback Jalen Hurts ruled out for the season, Philadelphia looks poised to finish with a losing record for the first time in head coach Nick Sirianni's six-year tenure with the team.

articles.title: Travis Etienne Jr. Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Saints RB's Return Timeline from IR
articles.summary: New Orleans Saints running back Travis Etienne Jr.'s five-game absence reportedly may come to an end Sunday.
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints running back Travis Etienne Jr.'s five-game absence reportedly may come to an end Sunday.

According to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer, the Saints plan to activate Etienne from injured reserve, putting him in line to play against the NFC South rival Carolina Panthers on Sunday afternoon.

Etienne had been out of action since suffering a hamstring injury during a Week 3 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.

After racking up 1,399 total yards from scrimmage and 13 touchdowns with the Jacksonville Jaguars last season, Etienne cashed in by signing a four-year, $47.4 million contract with the Saints in free agency.

Sharing the backfield with Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller, Etienne was off to a relatively slow start through his first three games with New Orleans, rushing for 128 yards and no touchdowns on 30 carries, while also catching 11 passes for 51 yards.

While Etienne was not being used as an every-down back, his efficiency was solid, averaging 4.3 yards per carry, which matched the second-best average of his career from last season.

The 27-year-old Etienne is now set to rejoin what remains a crowded backfield with Kamara and Audric Estimé in the mix. Miller was released by New Orleans last week.

It would be fair to expect head coach Kellen Moore to re-integrate Etienne slowly given the nature of the injury he is returning from and how much it can impact a running back.

However, based on the contract Etienne signed with the Saints, one can only assume the team's preference moving forward is for him to be the primary back with Kamara and Estimé providing support.

The Panthers represent a soft landing spot for Etienne should he indeed return to the lineup on Sunday, as they rank 28th in the NFL against the run this season.

articles.title: Kenneth Walker Injured, Latest Rumors on Chiefs RB vs. Falcons and Emmett Johnson Fantasy Outlook
articles.summary: After being a late addition to the injury report on Friday, Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III won't play in Week 10.
articles.body:
After being a late addition to the injury report on Friday, Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III won't play in Week 10.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Chiefs are going to hold Walker out of Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons due to a groin injury because they "want to give him a week" rather than try to force him to play through it.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport added the injury is considered "minor" and the Chiefs want to exercise caution with Walker.

Week 10 Fantasy Injury Report and Last Minute Waiver Wire Replacements

From a fantasy perspective, Emmett Johnson should be a late addition to your roster on the waiver wire as he gets set to make his first career start. He is only rostered in 33 percent of leagues right now, per FantasyPros .

Johnson was arguably the best player on the field for the Chiefs two weeks ago in their 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos. He had 128 receiving yards and one touchdown on five receptions, as well as one carry for 15 yards in just 13 offensive snaps.

Even though Atlanta's defense has been strong against the run, ranking third in EPA per rush, the ability Johnson showed as a receiver significantly boosts his fantasy value.

Chiefs head coach Andy Reid told reporters after Friday's practice that Walker had a "tight groin" when he showed up for practice, so the team held him out as a precaution.

"We'll see how he feels through this afternoon, with rehab, and through tomorrow," Reid said.

It's unclear exactly when or how the injury happened since Walker was not included on the Chiefs' official injury report prior to Friday.

Walker's absence creates a huge void for Kansas City's offense. He has started all eight games so far this season, ranking second in rushing yards (872) and seventh in rushing attempts (159). His five 100-yard rushing games and 109.0 rushing yards per game lead the NFL.

Johnson shouldn't be expected to handle the similar workload as Walker, but he can be used in many different ways to help make things easier for Patrick Mahomes. His 14 receptions rank sixth on the Chiefs despite playing just 134 offensive snaps.

Among all running backs with at least 25 carries, Johnson's success rate of 46.15 percent ranks ninth, ahead of Kyren Williams and James Cook.

The Chiefs likely want to avoid testing Walker in part because their schedule gets very difficult soon. They have a five-game run starting on Thanksgiving Day against the Buffalo Bills, Los Angeles Rams, Cincinnati Bengals, New England Patriots and San Francisco 49ers.

Kansas City plays the Falcons in Atlanta on Sunday, followed by a home game against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 11.

articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors Reveal Tony Pollard Eyed by Super Bowl Contenders and Titans' Asking Price
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers and Denver Broncos were interested in acquiring Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard ahead of the NFL trade deadline, ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported on Saturday.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers and Denver Broncos were interested in acquiring Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard ahead of the NFL trade deadline, ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported on Saturday.

Neither team was willing to meet Tennessee's asking price of a third-round pick.

The Packers and Broncos are in contention for the Super Bowl, but the offenses for both teams have struggled to move the ball on the ground. Denver is ranked No. 24 with 823 rushing yards, while Green Bay is dead last among all teams with 614 rushing yards, per the NFL .

Pollard has 133 carries for 595 rushing yards and six touchdowns through eight games this season.

Pollard was selected in the fourth round of the 2019 draft by the Dallas Cowboys. He spent his first three seasons as a backup, but won the starting role after outperforming Ezekiel Elliott in 2022. Since then, Pollard has put together four straight 1,000-yard rushing seasons. At his current pace, he would finish this season with a career-high 1,190 rushing yards.

Tennessee's decision to keep Pollard came as a surprise. The 29-year-old running back is entering the final year of his three-year, $21.75 million contract and will be a free agent in March, per Spotrac . The Titans already showed they were willing to part with their best players when they agreed to a blockbuster trade that sent All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears in exchange for a haul of draft picks.

Instead, Pollard will finish his season in Tennessee, and Denver and Green Bay will have to make a postseason run without upgrading their backfields.

Packers running back Josh Jacobs has started just three games this season, and he only managed to gain 80 rushing yards on 36 carries — an average of 2.2 yards per carry. Jacobs is expected to miss a few games after undergoing surgery to repair a broken finger. Running back MarShawn Lloyd hasn't been much more effective in his eight games, but second-year running back Kaleb Johnson provided a spark with 14 carries for 68 yards against the New England Patriots in Week 9.

The Broncos have featured a three-man rotation that includes running backs J.K. Dobbins, Jonah Coleman and RJ Harvey. Dobbins took the bulk of the carries early in the season but saw his carries decrease after failing to reach 70 rushing yards through six games. Coleman has seen more opportunities in recent weeks, while Harvey has been featured in a pass-catching role.

articles.title: He was drafted as an NFL team’s future. It arrives now.
articles.summary: Fernando Mendoza, the Heisman-winning quarterback selected No. 1 overall in last year’s NFL draft, takes over as starter for the Las Vegas Raiders. Will he turn around the franchise?
articles.body: When Heisman Trophy-winning quarterback Fernando Mendoza was selected first overall by the Las Vegas Raiders in April’s NFL draft, he updated his biography on LinkedIn to say that he was “focused on preparation, growth and discipline.” Emphasis on the first part. It is a quirk of the NFL that teams historically race to draft a quarterback early, then play them as little as possible for much of their first season. Teams view the position as so demanding and the pro game so fast that they want their prized picks to prepare as much as possible before inheriting the pressure of an entire franchise. Mendoza’s time to prepare ended Tuesday, nine games into his rookie season. Now, the Raiders need him to produce. Before Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, Las Vegas (4-5) traded veteran starting quarterback Kirk Cousins and elevated Mendoza to starter ahead of Sunday’s Week 10 matchup against the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks (5-4). Cousins had thrown 20 touchdowns, the most by any quarterback to change teams midseason in NFL history, per NBC Sports research. After starting 3-0, the Raiders have lost five of their last six games but still have what one playoff tracker pegged this week as a 15% chance to make what would be only the franchise’s third playoff appearance since 2003. Trading Cousins and elevating Mendoza “is no way to signify that we are punting on the season or looking forward to 2027,” Raiders general manager John Spytek said. “It’s something that [Mendoza] worked very hard for since the moment he walked into this building,” Spytek told reporters this week. “He passed every test. I want to stop short of saying he’s earned it, but he put us in a position where we had to make a really hard decision today with his growth as a person, as a teammate, as a leader, as a quarterback.” Mendoza is known as a quick study. While attending Cal, he spent his summers away from Berkeley interning at investment firms. In his first and only season at Indiana last fall, Mendoza picked up the Hoosiers’ offensive playbook so quickly that he led the perennial Big Ten doormat to a stunning national championship by using his arms and his feet. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak, who as an offensive playcaller mentored Sam Darnold during last season’s Super Bowl run with the Seahawks, said that Cousins was “the right role model” for Mendoza to learn from and accelerate his acclimation to the NFL. “It’s time to rally around Fernando,” center Tyler Linderbaum said. “Everyone has to step up and play for him. Obviously, it’s never easy being a rookie in that first game, but there’s 10 other guys on the field with him, there’s a whole defense, special teams unit, and just be there for him. Let him play with confidence. We’ve seen it every day in practice, the plays he can make.” Mendoza’s only snaps to this point came Oct. 11 when he played late in a blowout loss to the New England Patriots and completed 6 of his 8 passes. Rookie debuts are inherently difficult; quarterbacks taken No. 1 overall are 5-23-1 in their first start since 1970, per NBC Sports research. Facing the Seahawks will make Mendoza’s big day even more challenging. Seattle leads the NFL in total defense, allowing just 244 yards per game. Mendoza might not be under the most pressure of any Raiders player on Sunday, however. The team’s defense has allowed 30 or more points in each of its last six games, tied for the longest streak by a team in a season in NFL history. “Fernando has done everything we’ve asked him to do in practice,” Kubiak said. “I think he’s exceeded those expectations, and we all know that live bullets Sunday is far different from practice. However, he showed us that he’s ready, not only physically, but mentally.”

Aaron Rodgers made amends with his family earlier this year, and the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback supported his brother on Friday.

Rodgers' brother, Jordan, was on the call for Friday's game between Pitt and Florida State for ESPN and ABC at Acrisure Stadium, and Rodgers posed for a photo with him, adding a heartwarming caption as well.
