articles.title: Shades of Maxx Crosby, Inside Broncos-Chargers Failed Daiyan Henley Trade Detailed in New NFL Rumors
articles.summary: Daiyan Henley was already in Denver when the trade between the Broncos and the Los Angeles Chargers was called off.
articles.body:
Daiyan Henley was already in Denver when the trade between the Broncos and the Los Angeles Chargers was called off .

According to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , Henley had already met with general manager George Paton, toured the facility and begun reviewing the Broncos' defensive playbook when Denver backed out of the deal.

Jones also noted that the linebacker has a known knee injury, though it hasn't required surgery or kept him out of games. Jones added, however, that "the medical information the Broncos received did not match what they were learning in real-time after consulting with their own medical team and an independent doctor," similar to the nixed trade between the Las Vegas Raiders and Baltimore Ravens for Maxx Crosby over the offseason.

NFL Rule Changes on Trade Deadline 'Snafus' and Schedule Eyed, New Rumors Reveal

The called-off deal between the Chargers and Broncos, which came after a handful of other nixed deals, could lead to "conversations with the league and competition committee about changes to the rules," according to Jones.

Tom Pelissero of The Ringer added more context about possible changes after the season:

"Multiple GMs I spoke with agreed the league and the competition committee should reexamine teams' ability to renegotiate trade terms once the deadline passes, arguing a team could abuse the system," he reported .

Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh called out the Broncos following the trade, saying the "loophole" that allowed them to back out of the trade should be looked into.

"The Broncos based a pass/fail on a medical grade based on whether we would take less compensation and we wouldn't, and we didn't," Harbaugh told reporters Thursday. "In my opinion, it's one of those loopholes that the league should really look into because it sets a bad precedent and continues to set a bad precedent."

"It's a loophole and teams should not have the ability to do that," he added. "It's a medical grade, it's a pass/fail for a medical grade. They told us they weren't gonna pass him if it was a fourth and a fifth, which was agreed upon, and they would not pass him for that. They would pass him for a fourth and fill in the blank. I don't know what to call that, but that's what it is."

While the Chargers weren't sellers at the deadline despite their disastrous start to the season, Jones noted that they were willing to trade their team captain to the Broncos with the "hope that they could actually re-sign him come March." Henley, 26, will be a free agent at the end of the season.

Ultimately, they'll keep Henley around for the remainder of the year at least, albeit at the expense of losing some draft capital from the Broncos backing out of the deal.

articles.title: Jonathan Taylor's Trade Value Questioned by NFL Insiders After Colts Rejected Deal at 2026 Deadline
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts opted not to trade star running back Jonathan Taylor despite a fire sale at the deadline, and that decision could come back to haunt them.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts opted not to trade star running back Jonathan Taylor despite a fire sale at the deadline, and that decision could come back to haunt them.

According to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , Taylor's value could decrease from now to the end of the season, when he is expected to be on the trade block again.

"League sources aren't sure a deal of a second and fifth will be on the table for Taylor in March, so it could be easy to say Indy should have dealt him this past week," Jones reported.

The Colts traded a number of top players before the deadline, including Josh Downs, Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner and Keenan Allen. Many expected them to deal Taylor and potentially even quarterback Daniel Jones, but they ultimately held on to both.

Jones noted that the Colts "weren't high" on trading Jones as they look for him to return to pre-Achilles tear form. With Jones staying in Indianapolis, he needed a "quality running back" in Taylor, according to Jones.

The decision not to trade Taylor and Jones could pay off since it will give Indianapolis two offensive pieces to build around, but if the Colts decide to trade Taylor over the offseason, it may end up being a missed opportunity.

Jones had a career year in Indianapolis in 2025 before tearing his Achilles, but he's struggled in 2026, throwing for 1,722 yards, six touchdowns and 10 interceptions amid a 2-7 start to the campaign.

Taylor, on the other hand, has still put up good numbers despite the team's overall struggles. He's recorded the eighth-most rushing yards (656) and the sixth-most touchdowns (8) while adding 220 yards through the air.

Taylor's continued success made him a hot commodity on the trade market, but the Colts thought better of dealing him. He'll be 28 next offseason, though, which will naturally lead to a drop in his market.

Whether Indianapolis will move on from him after the season remains to be seen.

articles.title: NFL Rule Changes on Trade Deadline 'Snafus' and Schedule Eyed, New Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: Many within the NFL reportedly are hoping to enact rule changes regarding trade acceptance protocols and the positioning of the trade deadline.
articles.body:
Many within the NFL reportedly are hoping to enact rule changes regarding trade acceptance protocols and the positioning of the trade deadline.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the NFL's competition committee is expected to discuss potential alterations to the manner in which trades are agreed upon and executed after some "snafus" on deadline day.

The Cincinnati Bengals backed out of a trade for Philadelphia Eagles pass-rusher Arnold Ebiketie, and the Denver Broncos attempted to alter the compensation they agreed to in a trade for Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley that was ultimately nixed.

Additionally, according to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer, there is support among some in the NFL to push back the trade deadline an extra week, and there is a "good chance" the topic will be discussed in February and March when the competition committee meets.

The subject of rescinded trades is something that has been a hot topic of discussion since the offseason when the Baltimore Ravens backed out of a deal that would have landed them Las Vegas Raiders superstar pass-rusher Maxx Crosby.

Baltimore opted against completing the deal after Crosby underwent his physical, which is similar to what happened with Henley in Denver on Tuesday.

Per ESPN's Jeff Legwold , a knee issue was flagged during Henley's physical, which prompted the Broncos to approach the Chargers with a proposal to alter the trade compensation that was agreed upon.

The Chargers declined to do so, and Henley was returned to them, resulting in Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh speaking out about the turn of events.

Harbaugh told reporters this week, "The Broncos based a pass-fail on a medical grade, based on whether we would take less compensation. And we wouldn't. And we didn't. And in my opinion, it's one of those loopholes that the league should really look into because it sets a bad precedent, and it continues to set a bad precedent."

According to Schefter and Rapoport, multiple NFL front office executives expressed their belief this week that trade terms should not be negotiable once a deal is agreed upon.

Because of that, it is reportedly possible the competition committee could institute a new rule that would bar teams from trying to change the compensation after a concerning physical. The acquiring team would only have the option to accept or decline what was already agreed upon under those circumstances.

As for the trade deadline date, Pelissero spoke to 18 NFL general managers and executives anonymously this week, and eight of them supported the idea of moving the deadline back one week to the Tuesday after Week 10.

Seven general managers were fine with the deadline as is, one was fine with either option, one had no preference and one favored moving the deadline up one week.

Pelissero noted that at least 24 of the NFL's 32 owners would have to vote in favor of moving the deadline back a week in order for it to pass.

The decision to move the deadline back an extra week in 2024 was reportedly done with an eye from changing to a 16-game to a 17-game schedule, as the change kept the deadline nine weeks before the end of the season.

Because of that, Pelissero suggested the league may want to hold off on moving the deadline back another week until and unless the decision is made to move to an 18-game schedule.

articles.title: 'Panic' Kirk Cousins Trade, Fernando Mendoza as QB1 Addressed by Raiders in New NFL Rumors
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are not concerned about Fernando Mendoza's readiness to step in as their starting quarterback after trading Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders are not concerned about Fernando Mendoza's readiness to step in as their starting quarterback after trading Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings on Tuesday.

Appearing on the Saturday morning SportsCenter , ESPN's Jeremy Fowler explained the Cousins trade was not a "panic" move when a good offer came in because of how Mendoza has progressed over the course of the season:

"When I texted with people from the Las Vegas Raiders this week, is Fernando Mendoza ready? I got a quote, 'Definitely yes' multiple times. So, they felt like he was ready enough to where trading Kirk Cousins was not a panic move. Now, had Cousins stayed he probably would have remained the starter for at least Week 10, but they felt like nine games in, Mendoza had got himself ready because in the spring he spent significant time just trying to get the steps down in Gary Kubiak's offense with the play action, all the nuances. And then over time the last few months they tried to get him reps when they could in practice; he did really well with those, so he's passed every test. And they also feel like he's going to give them a little more athleticism. He can throw on the run, bigger arm than Kirk Cousins. So, they know he's going to make some mistakes as a rookie, but they feel like the upside is going to create potentially some more splash plays."

Kirk Trade Result of Vikings' 'Desperation'

The Raiders seemed like they were sticking to the plan of not having Mendoza start. Head coach Klint Kubiak emphasized there was " no controversy " and Cousins would remain No. 1 on the depth chart following a 35-21 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, their fourth consecutive defeat after a 3-0 start.

Their plans shifted when they were able to land a 2027 third-round pick from the Vikings for Cousins.

Raiders players and coaches don't seem at all worried about Mendoza being overwhelmed.

Quarterbacks coach Mike Sullivan told ESPN's Ryan McFadden about the extra work Mendoza has been doing on his own to prepare himself.

"He literally walks through the play and goes through what his reads [are], his pre-snap communication [and] footwork," Sullivan said. "His command of the offense, his ability to articulate the huddle calls [and] communicate at the line of scrimmage, has improved consistently. It's certainly credit to him."

Mendoza has only appeared in one game so far this season. He played 10 snaps in garbage time of the Raiders' 45-17 loss to the New England Patriots in Week 5, completing six of his eight attempts for 48 yards.

Now, Mendoza will make his first career start with an extremely difficult matchup against the Seattle Seahawks defense. The No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL draft has never lacked confidence or belief in his ability, a trait that will serve him well as he gets acclimated to the NFL.

Kubiak told McFadden the Raiders don't expect Mendoza to do more than he needs to against the Seahawks because the offense as a whole is there to support him.

"Every week in the NFL is tough, and this is the best defense in the NFL," Kubiak said. "Again, he's got to do his job and not worry about a whole lot else. Everybody does their one-eleventh, and everyone around him elevates their play."

With the Raiders having lost five of six games following their 3-0 start, it's probably in their best interest to let Mendoza get as much playing time as possible now so they know what he needs to work on.

It's also not out of the question Mendoza could help lead the Raiders to the playoffs. They have a good offensive infrastructure to support the rookie with Kubiak calling plays and Brock Bowers as his primary outlet at tight end.

The Raiders (4-5) are only one game behind the Patriots for the final playoff spot going into Week 10.

articles.title: Dan Quinn's Hot Seat Updated by Commanders Insider in New NFL Rumors After Win vs. Harbaugh, Giants
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders' win over the New York Giants on Thursday might have saved head coach Dan Quinn's job.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders' win over the New York Giants on Thursday might have saved head coach Dan Quinn's job.

With the win, the Commanders got back into the NFC East race, as their 3-5-1 record puts them just two games behind the Giants. According to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , the team has full trust in Quinn for now.

"This thing is wide open," a Commanders source said, per Jones. "DQ isn't losing this locker room."

Quinn had a tremendous first season in Washington, leading the Commanders to a 12-5 finish and their first NFC Championship Game appearance since 1991, but a 5-12 record last year perhaps started hot-seat conversations.

The Commanders then started the 2026 campaign 1-4-1 and had some questionable coaching decisions along the way, which only increased hot-seat buzz for Quinn.

Washington has now won two of its last three games, though, and is back in the playoff mix thanks to a relatively weak NFC East.

The Giants still sit in first place in the division at 5-3-1, but they have a tough schedule moving forward after a relatively easy start to the season. New York will finish off the season facing teams like the Jacksonville Jaguars, the San Francisco 49ers, the Seattle Seahawks and the Detroit Lions.

The Commanders have a much easier back half of the schedule, with the Bengals, Vikings and Jaguars being their only opponents that are currently about .500 on the year.

The 4-5 Dallas Cowboys are also still in the mix for the NFC East crown, though, so the Commanders still have lots of work to do.

If Quinn can overcome the rough start and get Washington back into the playoffs, it's fair to assume he'll earn at least another year at the helm. If things get worse, however, he might be out of a job at the end of the season.

articles.title: Kyler Murray Injury Update, New NFL Rumors on Vikings QB's Return Timeline After Kirk Cousins Trade
articles.summary: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray is still "a couple of weeks away" from returning from his Grade 2 hamstring strain, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported on Saturday.
articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray is still "a couple of weeks away" from returning from his Grade 2 hamstring strain, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported on Saturday.

The 29-year-old quarterback could be targeting Minnesota's Week 12 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons for his potential return, according to Pelissero.

Murray's absence doesn't seem as urgent after the Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for a third-round draft pick. If Cousins misses time, the team will have to turn to Carson Wentz, who is serving as the backup in Murray's absence.

Murray suffered the injury during a 19-15 loss against the Detroit Lions in Week 8. He also missed Week 2 after suffering a concussion in Minnesota's regular-season opener.

Although Murray compiled a 5-1 record as a starter this season, he was at the helm of a struggling Vikings offense. The eighth-year quarterback has just 1,022 passing yards with five touchdowns and three interceptions.

Wentz struggled mightily when he stepped in for Murray on Monday night against the Buffalo Bills. He completed just 32 percent of his passes for 81 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions.

Minnesota showed interest in reuniting with Cousins prior to Monday night , but Wentz' poor performance likely made it easier for the Vikings to name Cousins as the starter for a pivotal matchup against the Green Bay Packers in Week 10.

Cousins is already familiar with head coach Kevin O'Connell's offensive system from the last two seasons of his six-year stint in Minnesota. He also has plenty of chemistry with star wide receiver Justin Jefferson, who enjoyed his most productive years on the receiving end of Cousins' passes.

Cousins and O'Connell both struggled after parting ways, but they now have an opportunity to make up for lost time. Still, Murray's availability could prove valuable behind a 38-year-old quarterback.

Until then, the backup role will go to Wentz, and second-year quarterback Max Brosmer will serve as the emergency No. 3 option.

articles.title: NFL: Fernando Mendoza set for 'baptism of fire' as No 1 pick makes first start for Las Vegas Raiders against against Seattle Seahawks
articles.summary: Fernando Mendoza, the No 1 pick at the 2026 NFL Draft, will make his first start for the Las Vegas Raiders this Sunday when he takes over from the departed Kirk Cousins against the Seattle Seahawks; watch live on Sky Sports+ from 9.05pm
articles.body:
The NFL's No 1 overall draft pick will make his first regular-season start this Sunday when he takes the reins at quarterback for Klint Kubiak's side.

Mendoza will lead the Raiders out against the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks following the departure of Kirk Cousins in a deadline day trade back to the Minnesota Vikings.

The Heisman Trophy winner has spent the entire summer and the first half of the season learning behind his veteran mentor. Now the stage is his, against the best defense in football.

"This Seattle Seahawks defense, despite having a couple of losses, is still phenomenal," said Sky Sports NFL's Phoebe Schecter on Inside the Huddle.

"They really have a similar kind of DNA to the Vikings, especially for a rookie. You know exactly what you're going to do against this young man.

"You look at Nick Emmanwori and how as a quarterback you stand back there and have to figure out who's coming, who's not, where, what, who is playing what position.

"And then that defensive line, telling him to keep his eyes up the whole time. This is going to be a lot of hand-holding, I would suggest, for this first game, and definitely a baptism by fire."

It beckons as a reunion for Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak, who served as offensive coordinator of the Sam Darnold, Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Kenneth Walker-led unit that won the Super Bowl in February.

He helped inspire the best of Darnold amid his career resurrection, and is now tasked with orchestrating a smooth start to the career of a young quarterback.

"Our expectation is for him to lead the offense, to lead the operation, and to go play a game here Sunday and be the leader of the team," said Kubiak

"We have to prepare him and give him a lot of reps to get him comfortable."

Mendoza's only action this season came in October when he made a fourth-quarter cameo in the Raiders' 45-17 defeat to the Patriots, going six of eight for 48 yards.

"This is something that he's worked very hard for since the moment he walked into this building," said Raiders general manager John Spytek.

"He passed every test. He put us in a position where we had to make a very hard decision today with his growth as a person, as a teammate, as a leader, as a quarterback."

Mendoza was selected with the first pick of the draft in April after guiding the unbeaten Indiana Hoosiers to their first college national title while throwing for 3,535 yards and 41 touchdowns with a completion percentage of 72.

"It's a bit challenging because you have no tape on him," said Seahawks defensive tackle Byron Murphy II. "You don't have too many tendencies or some of his weaknesses.

"As far as what I've seen on tape, the guy, number one draft pick, he can make all the throws. As a unit, as a defense, especially as a defensive line, we can get after this guy, especially in the passing game. We have to rush as one, be on one accord and our communication has to be at a high level. We can get after him."

Mendoza takes over an offense ranked 15th in total yards, fifth in passing and eighth in scoring after an impressive start to the campaign from 38-year-old Cousins, who has thrown for a fifth-most 2,340 yards and 20 touchdowns to eight interceptions. Such has been his impact that the Vikings sought to re-acquire the quarterback in a bid to solve their offensive slump.

Brock Bowers looms as Mendoza's top target with a team-high 658 receiving yards and six touchdowns while averaging 94.0 yards per game.

The Raiders sit 4-5 as they prepare to take on the 5-4 Seahawks, who will again be led by Drew Lock in his second successive start in place of the injured Darnold.

articles.title: 'Nefarious' Concern Addressed by NFL Insider After Bengals Called Off Trade with Eagles for Ebiketie
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals were set to acquire defensive end Arnold Ebiketie from the Philadelphia Eagles ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, but ultimately called the deal off before it was finalized.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals were set to acquire defensive end Arnold Ebiketie from the Philadelphia Eagles ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, but ultimately called the deal off before it was finalized.

The Bengals decided not to go through with the deal after realizing that they could lose a compensatory draft pick by acquiring Ebiketie. Tom Pelissero of The Ringer explained what Cincinnati's "mistake" was in the deal:

"The Bengals' mistake was agreeing to acquire Ebiketie for a 2027 sixth-round pick before checking with the NFL Management Council about how he would be counted. Once the deal was in place, the Bengals did call the league and got clarity: Because of one of many quirks in the formula, trading for Ebiketie—who signed a one-year, $4.3 million deal with the Eagles in March—would cause him to count as a free agent gain for both the Eagles and the Bengals, even though he's on a minimum salary for the rest of the season."

NFL Rule Changes on Trade Deadline 'Snafus' and Schedule Eyed, New Rumors Reveal

The process for determining compensatory picks is a complex one that Pelissero noted even the league office has gotten wrong in the past. Essentially, if a team gains fewer qualifying unrestricted free agents than it loses, it will receive compensatory picks.

While Pelissero noted that neither team acted "nefariously" while making the deal, "the blame is on the Bengals for agreeing first and asking questions later."

"Philly was a great trade partner," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor told reporters . "It was on our end."

articles.title: Inside Kirk Cousins' Contract and Impact on Vikings in 2027 Revealed in New NFL Rumors After Trade
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings may find offensive stability and consistency this season with quarterback Kirk Cousins at the helm, but their long-term plans at the position remain murky.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings may find offensive stability and consistency this season with quarterback Kirk Cousins at the helm, but their long-term plans at the position remain murky.

Minnesota's trade for Cousins "guarantees" that the team will be looking for another starting quarterback next spring, according to ESPN's Kevin Seifert .

The Las Vegas Raiders signed the 38-year-old quarterback to a one-year, $11.3 million contract prior to the season, but the language in the deal is a bit more complicated. On paper, Cousins' deal is five years for $172 million, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Along with a $10 million roster bonus for 2027 that is fully guaranteed, the contract includes a two-year club option worth $80 million that becomes fully guaranteed if Cousins is on the team on the fifth day of the league year in March. The last two years of the deal are void years.

If the rest of the season goes well, Minnesota could pick up the two-year option to keep Cousins on the team through 2028, but that's unlikely given the $80 million price tag. If the Vikings aren't able to sign Cousins to a new contract prior to the option kicking in, they'll have to release him.

The savvy veteran is notorious for not taking a discount. That's evident by his $333 million in career earnings , which have passed Tom Brady for fourth-most in NFL history.

articles.title: Cam Skattebo Explains Why He Threw Up During Giants' Loss to Commanders
articles.summary: Cam Sakattebo had his best game of the season on Thursday against the Washington Commanders, but it also featured a mid-game vomit on the sideline.
articles.body:
Cam Sakattebo had his best game of the season on Thursday against the Washington Commanders, but it also featured a mid-game vomit on the sideline.

The New York Giants running back threw up between the first and second quarters of the loss to the Commanders, according to Kaylee Hartung of the Prime Video Broadcast (h/t Natasha Dye of People ).

The culprit for his sickness was something you'd find at a county fair.

"Yeah, I had a pretzel-wrapped hot dog," Skattebo told reporters after the game. "Didn't sit right in the stomach."

Despite having to take a moment to get rid of his dinner, Skattebo put together a strong game with 78 rushing yards, 44 receiving yards and two touchdowns.

Next week, he'll look to keep his pregame meal a bit lighter.

articles.title: How the Chicago Bears grade at midway point of 2026
articles.summary: USA Today shared their midseason grade for the Chicago Bears after the first nine weeks of the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears are sitting in a good position at the midway point of the 2026 season, where they've won four straight, have a 7-2 record and sit in first place in an ultra competitive NFC North.

It's been an impressive start to the season for the Bears , who have lost just two games despite being without starting quarterback Caleb Williams for three games. Chicago also just played three consecutive prime-time games, going 4-0 in prime time in the first nine weeks of the season. The Bears' only losses have come to division rivals ( Minnesota Vikings , Green Bay Packers ) in what's been an historically great start for the NFC North.

USA Today's Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz shared his midseason grades for every NFL team, and the Bears were among the highest-graded teams through the first nine games. Chicago received an A- for their hot start, as well as Caleb Williams' solid performance and the acquisition of All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.

Photos from the Bears' ugly 27-24 win over Bucs in Week 9

With Caleb Williams coming into his own, anything feels possible for Chicago. An already sky-high ceiling was pushed even higher with the trade for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who changes the entire complexion of the unit he just joined. Williams' four interceptions in an unnecessarily close call against the Buccaneers emphasized the volatility that might be in play for this team, but the Bears look capable of leaning on their defense in key stretches rather than relying on Ben Johnson's machine-like offense not to have its gears get jammed every once in a while.

But things aren't going to get easier for Chicago down the stretch. The Bears have the most difficult remaining schedule in the NFL, where their easiest games are against the New Orleans Saints and Miami Dolphins . They also have four remaining division games (two against the Detroit Lions and one each against the Packers and Vikings), as well as AFC matchups against the Buffalo Bills and Jacksonville Jaguars .

It'll certainly be a big test for Ben Johnson's squad in their pursuit for a return to the postseason, but they have the talent in all phases to get it done.

articles.title: Seahawks announce captains for NFL Week 10 vs Raiders
articles.summary: Seattle will feature two new captains for their showdown with the Raiders.
articles.body:
The 5-4 Seattle Seahawks are aiming to secure another win before their Bye Week, and they will have to do so against the 4-5 Las Vegas Raiders . Their former AFC West foes started the season 3-0, but have lost five out of their last six games. Still, there is a bit of a Wild Card element given the fact Vegas will be starting rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza in his first ever game at the NFL level.

The Seahawks do not pick captains for the whole season. Instead, they rotate captains each week. We are officially at the point where we will see repeat captains on a more regular basis, however, this week features two new captains.

The only "repeat" captain is linebacker Drake Thomas, who was a captain in Week 2 earlier this year. Drew Lock and George Holani are both first timers this season.
